t: Leaving Room for Love: Remembering Others in Our Blessing
v: “‘When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not wholly reap the corners of your field, neither shall you gather the gleaning of your harvest.
You shall not strip your vineyard bare, neither shall you gather the fallen fruit of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am Yahweh your God.’”
“‘If a stranger lives with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.
The stranger who lives with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you were strangers in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.’”
b: God cares not only about our reverence for him and our keeping of his statutes, but also deeply about how we treat the vulnerable around us: the poor, the sojourner, the foreigner. He commanded his people not to reap the corners of their fields or gather what was left behind, not to encourage waste, but to teach a way of life that “leaves something for others.”

This attitude is a selfless choice: letting go of total control over our possessions, not keeping the whole harvest for ourselves, but deliberately leaving room for others to share. Such a life truly reflects the image of God: kindness, fairness, and the humility of remembering that we too were once sojourners in Egypt.
a: Leave a “corner of the field” in your life for those in need
Whether it is time, money, or resources, do not use it all up. Learn to leave room, to open the door for those who lack, and to leave space to respond to God’s work.
See the sojourner and the marginalized, and treat them with love
Do not care only for people like yourself, but see those from different backgrounds and in hard circumstances, and reach out and welcome them, because we too were once “sojourners.”
Write “I am Yahweh your God” on your heart
Every choice and action is not for moral achievement but because we belong to God. As he has shown grace to us, so we show grace to others.
q: Am I used to using up all my resources, leaving no room for those in need?
How do I regard people “outside my circle”? Am I willing to put the command to love my neighbor as myself into practice?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing me that true faith is not all for oneself, but is willing to leave room of blessing for others. Help me learn selfless love, giving thanks not only in times of harvest but also showing Your heart in sharing. May I love my neighbor as myself, as You have loved me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Selfless Path of a Disciple: Take Up the Cross and Walk into True Life
v: From that time, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and be raised the third day.
Peter took him aside, and began to rebuke him, saying, “Far be it from you, Lord! This will never be done to you.”
But he turned, and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”
Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life for my sake will find it.
For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will render to everyone according to his deeds.
Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.”
b: Jesus began to reveal his mission openly to his disciples: he would go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed, and be raised on the third day. Such a prophecy was shocking, and it collided with the disciples’ expectations. Out of love, Peter took Jesus aside and tried to stop him from taking the road of suffering. But Jesus sharply rebuked him: “You are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.” He reminded Peter that the path of discipleship is not to avoid self-denial, but to follow his example and take up one’s own cross to follow him.

Jesus’ words challenge the core of every believer’s faith: “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself.” This is not a forced sacrifice, but a deliberate surrender: laying down our authority to run our own lives, and letting God’s purpose reign within us. Selflessness is the beginning of true freedom; taking up the cross is the door into true life.
a: Adjust your focus

From the human viewpoint to God’s purpose. Peter’s reaction came from love, but it overlooked the greatness of God’s plan of redemption. Do you also often measure God’s ways by human logic? Before each choice, learn to ask, “What is God’s will?”
Practice selflessness

Letting go of self-centered control. Selflessness does not mean disappearing, but no longer putting yourself at the center. Learn to let God lead your schedule, plans, and decisions, and you will experience deeper trust and freedom.
Take up the cross

Bravely face the mission God entrusts to you. The cross is not only a symbol of suffering but a mark of obedience and love. What are you willing to give up for God’s Kingdom? Are you willing to keep walking the road of fulfilling his will?
q: In what matters do I often set my mind on my own will and overlook God’s heart?
Am I willing to choose selflessness every day and hand the authority back to God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing me the way of selflessness through Jesus. Help me let go of my habit of running my own life, learn to obey Your will, and bravely take up my cross to follow You. Because I choose selflessness, may I receive the truly abundant life You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Holding Fast to a Heart for Truth in a Deceived World
v: For the mystery of lawlessness is already working. Only there is one who restrains now, until he is taken out of the way.
Then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord will kill with the breath of his mouth, and bring to nothing by the brightness of his coming.
The coming of the lawless one is according to the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,
and with all deceit of wickedness for those who perish, because they didn’t receive the love of the truth, that they might be saved.
Because of this, God sends them a working of error, that they should believe a lie,
that they all might be judged who didn’t believe the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.
b: Paul reminded believers that before the Lord’s return, “the mystery of lawlessness” is already at work. He described a “lawless one” who will be revealed, performing all kinds of power, signs, and lying wonders to lure people away from the truth. Such deception is not accidental, but a planned work of Satan, aimed at those who “didn’t receive the love of the truth.”

This passage shows us that the key to faith is not whether you have ever heard the truth, but whether you “love the truth.” Many people choose wonder in front of miracles but not repentance, choose to believe a lie but are unwilling to know the truth. Real safety does not come from human protection, but from the Lord who can destroy the wicked one with the breath of his mouth. Our only way out is to humble ourselves under God’s word and sovereignty.

This is exactly the selfless choice: not making ourselves the judge of truth, but letting God be the standard and guide of our lives. In these confusing last days, only by loving the truth, trusting God, and letting him be King can we stand firm.
a: Discernment comes not from feelings but from truth
Do not look only at the surface of signs and wonders, but return to the Bible and use God’s word as the standard for telling right from wrong.
To love truth is to learn to obey it
It is not only liking to hear words that “suit me,” but being willing to be pruned and adjusted by the truth. This is real selflessness and humility.
Build inner vigilance and spiritual conviction
When deception and injustice fill the world, ask the Lord to strengthen our hearts so that we do not drift with the tide, but walk in the light and make decisions as God guides.
q: Do I merely “hear the truth” without really “loving the truth”?
Am I willing to let God’s word guide me, rather than acting on feelings or trends?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, in these confusing last days, give me a heart that loves the truth, so that I can discern deception and stand firm. Help me rely not on what I see or feel, but cling to Your word and Your holy guidance. May my life be filled with reverence and obedience, so that I am not one who believes a lie, but holds fast to the true way until the Lord returns. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Living by Faith: Choosing Obedience Without Seeing
v: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
For by this, the elders obtained testimony.
By faith, we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made out of things which are visible.

By faith, Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he had testimony given to him that he was righteous, God testifying with respect to his gifts; and through it he, being dead, still speaks.

By faith, Enoch was taken away, so that he wouldn’t see death, and he was not found, because God translated him. For he has had testimony given to him that before his translation he had been well pleasing to God.
Without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to him, for he who comes to God must believe that he exists, and that he is a rewarder of those who seek him.

By faith, Noah, being warned by God about things not yet seen, moved with godly fear, prepared a ship for the saving of his house, through which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is according to faith.
By faith, Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to a place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.
b: Faith is “assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.” This sentence not only sets the theme for all of Hebrews 11, but also marks out a clear path for our journey of faith: not by sight, not by control, but by faith moving toward God’s promises.

From Abel, Enoch, and Noah to Abraham, these spiritual forebears all made choices of “already believing” in circumstances of “not yet seeing.” Their faith was not passive waiting but active response. Their actions did not come from their own opinions but from trusting God’s word and character. What they valued was “God’s pleasure,” not the applause of the world or the safety in front of them.

Such faith is in fact a selfless choice. No longer relying on visible security, we place the future in God’s hands. Such faith also puts into practice letting God be King, following his principles, and obeying his guidance, building up a life within God’s divine order.
a: Choose to follow God’s call when you cannot see
Abraham “went out, not knowing where he went,” yet set out by faith. You can do the same, responding to God’s leading in faith even when the road ahead is unclear.
Put faith into action in daily life
Noah prepared an ark by faith, even when there was no rain. His actions testified to the reality of his faith. Today you too can live by faith in your family, workplace, and church.
Faith is the key to pleasing God
Hebrews reminds us: “Without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing to him.” When you are willing to lay yourself down, lean on God, and seek his will, you are walking the road to his pleasure.
q: Am I willing to take the first step in faith before I see the result?
Do I treat faith as action, and not merely as an idea?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for opening, through faith, the way for us to walk with You. Help me to choose to believe before I see, and to choose obedience when things seem confusing. Give me the faith of Abraham, the reverence of Noah, and the intimacy of Enoch, so that I may live a life that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: People of the Day: Staying Alert, Sober, and Building One Another Up
v: But you, brothers, aren’t in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief.
You are all children of light, and children of the day. We don’t belong to the night, nor to darkness,
so then let’s not sleep, as the rest do, but let’s watch and be sober.
For those who sleep, sleep in the night, and those who are drunken are drunken in the night.
But let us, since we belong to the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation.
For God didn’t appoint us to wrath, but to the obtaining of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who died for us, that whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him.
Therefore exhort one another, and build each other up, even as you also do.
But we beg you, brothers, to know those who labor among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you,
and to respect and honor them in love for their work’s sake. Be at peace among yourselves.
We exhort you, brothers, admonish the disorderly, encourage the faint-hearted, support the weak, be patient toward all.
See that no one returns evil for evil to anyone, but always follow after that which is good, for one another, and for all.
b: Paul reminded believers: “You aren’t in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief.” This is not a warning but a confirmation of identity. We are people of the light and of the day, no longer belonging to night and darkness, so we should live in a way that fits that identity: staying alert and sober, encouraging one another, not sleeping, neglecting, or hurting each other.

The point of this passage is not predicting the end times but daily practice. God did not appoint us to wrath, but to obtain salvation through his Anointed One. Because of this salvation, we put on faith and love as a breastplate and the hope of salvation as a helmet, turning truth into a mindset lived out in life: letting God’s standard guard our thinking, God’s example guide our actions, and God’s Spirit fill us with hope.

Believers do not fight alone; we are a community that builds one another up. We learn to respect leaders, encourage the discouraged, support the weak, and mark ourselves by patience and kindness toward each other. This is a concrete way of “letting God be King”: not ruling ourselves, but letting love and truth rule in the community.
a: Put on spiritual armor and live out your identity in the light
Each morning you can declare in faith: “I am a child of light. Today I will guard my heart with faith and love, and guard my mind with hope.”
Choose to build one another up rather than attack one another
When you disagree with someone, choose to encourage, admonish, and support, rather than criticize, withdraw, or retaliate. This is living out a selfless life.
Evaluate people and things by God’s standard
Do not judge by emotion or the world’s measure alone. Learn to see leaders, community, and your own role through the eyes of the Bible, and walk in the light.
q: Am I living in the light, or do I sometimes still let dark emotions or behavior take charge?
Recently, in some matter, have I chosen humility and selflessness rather than argument or revenge?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for making me no longer belong to the night, but to the light. Help me put on the armor of faith, hope, and love every day, relying not on myself but on Your word as my standard. Help me also to live out building one another up in community, treating each brother and sister with patience and love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Blessing of God’s Presence: From Worship into Abundant Rest
v: I will sing a new song to you, God. On a ten-stringed lyre, I will sing praises to you.
You are he who gives salvation to kings, who rescues David your servant from the deadly sword.
Rescue me, and deliver me from the hand of foreigners, whose mouth speaks deceit, whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
Then our sons will be like plants grown up in their youth, our daughters like pillars carved for a palace.
Our barns are full, filled with all kinds of provision. Our sheep bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our fields.
Our oxen will pull heavy loads. There is no breaking in, and no going away, and no outcry in our streets.
Happy are the people who are in such a situation. Happy are the people whose God is Yahweh.
b: David sang out in great praise: “I will sing a new song to you, God.” This song is not only melody and notes, but a response to and declaration of God’s works. He praised the God who saves kings, who in danger reached out to rescue his servant from enemies and lies. It is a testimony to God’s sovereignty and faithfulness, and also a humble, selfless attitude: knowing that peace is not achieved by ourselves, but that abundance is lived out through the grace God gives.

David’s prayer did not stop at personal salvation but extended to the whole of society and family. He saw children growing strong, barns full, flocks multiplying, peace in the city, and harmony in society. These are the results of God’s blessing and rule. This is also a true picture of “letting God be King”: when the people obey God and make him the center, the whole order enters into harmony and prosperity.

This is a view of life in which “worship brings forth governance.” Peace is not earned by effort, but is the result of fearing God and relying on him. “Happy are the people whose God is Yahweh!” This is the attitude of a life that acknowledges God and honors him as great, a blessing that moves from “selflessness” into “his presence.”
a: Worship with a new song and open the eyes of faith
Even before you see the harvest, peace, or change, you can first praise God’s faithfulness with a new song. Worship is not because circumstances are favorable, but a choice to honor him in faith.
Place your family and society under God’s rule
Bring your children, work, and city in prayer, asking God to be the King who brings order and blessing. Do not try to hold everything together by yourself, but let God take charge.
Live out a blessed order, starting from God and extending to people

Do not first ask for full barns and peace, but first for worship and surrender. Let your family, church, and workplace, because of your obedience to God, bring out the blessing of “Yahweh is their God.”
q: Do I make worship the starting point of my life? What one thing am I willing to hand back to God’s rule, letting him reign over it?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I will sing a new song to You, for You are the God who saves kings and the true source of my trust. Help me place my family and my life in Your hands, so that I do not grasp peace by my own strength, but experience Your rule and blessing in worship and obedience. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Hearing and Obeying Is More Blessed Than Seeing Miracles
v: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice, and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”
But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah, the prophet.
For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so will also the Son of Man be to this generation.

The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, someone greater than Jonah is here.”
b: While Jesus was teaching the crowd, a woman sincerely praised his mother: “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!” But Jesus replied, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.” He showed that true blessing does not come from a physical relationship with him, but from a real connection with God’s word: hearing it and obeying it.

This reminds us that the core of faith is not chasing outward experiences or miracles, but inner repentance and obedience. As Jesus went on to say, this generation kept seeking signs, yet God had already made Jonah a sign to the Ninevites, and now God himself had come among people in his Son: “someone greater than Jonah is here,” “one greater than Solomon is here.” The greatest sign is the Lord Jesus himself. His word, his death, and his resurrection are God’s greatest revelation to humanity.

If we seek only feelings and experiences but neglect actually keeping God’s word, we are like that evil generation, wanting proof for our eyes but unwilling to repent in our hearts. But when we choose to submit, listen, and practice, we enter into true blessing.
a: Value God’s word more deeply than miracles
Miracles pass away, but God’s word will never pass away. Are you willing to read, reflect, and practice every day, letting the Word become the foundation of your life?
Repentance and obedience are the door to miracles
Just as the Ninevites repented when they heard Jonah’s message, we should listen to the word with reverence, not only receiving it but doing it.
Acknowledge that Jesus is greater than everything and let him rule your life

Whether wise like Solomon or powerful like Jonah, none compare with the salvation and truth of Jesus. He not only speaks the word, he is the Word. Letting him be King of your life is the beginning of true blessing.
q: Do I long more for outward experiences and overlook putting God’s word into practice? How can I respond to Jesus’ words today to make my faith more real?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, help me not to stop at hearing the word, but to be one who puts Your word into practice in daily life. I do not want to chase only feelings and experiences, but to seek Your will with a single heart and live a life that pleases You. May my repentance and obedience be a true blessing in Your eyes. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Fan the Gift into Flame and Boldly Witness to the Lord’s Name
v: For this cause, I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner, but endure hardship with the Good News according to the power of God,
who saved us, and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and brought life and incorruption to light through the Good News,
to which I was appointed a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
For this cause I suffer these things. Yet I am not ashamed, for I know him whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to guard that which I have committed to him against that day.
Hold the pattern of sound words which you have heard from me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
That good thing which was committed to you, guard through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
b: These words from Paul to Timothy are like the heartfelt charge of a spiritual father to his son. He reminded Timothy not to let the gift God gave him fall silent, but to “stir it up” like a fire. The gift here is not merely a display of ability, but a calling and mission entrusted by God. What enables this gift to come alive is not human courage, but the spirit of power, love, and self-control that God gives.

Paul set himself as an example. Though imprisoned for preaching the Good News, he was not ashamed at all, but said with full confidence, “I know him whom I have believed!” This confidence is no empty encouragement; it comes from a deep knowledge of God’s grace, salvation, and trust. He urged Timothy, and urges us as well, to hold fast to the true faith we have received through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.

On the road of faith we often meet trials, persecution, pressure, and confusion, but God has not called us to fear; he has called us to stand firm. When we choose a selfless faith, letting Jesus be King and his word our standard, we will experience the incorruptible life revealed within us.
a: Fan into flame again the gift God gave you

God may have called you to certain gifts through prayer, revelation, or service. Do not let them be forgotten or buried. Ask God to light the fire in your heart once more, and bravely answer his call.
Hold to the true faith through the Holy Spirit, not by sheer endurance

This generation is full of voices and values. Only by the Holy Spirit can we keep the pattern of sound words. It is not by our own strength, but by the God who dwells within us that we are made strong.
Do not be ashamed, but take pride in preaching the Good News

Whatever your setting, whether workplace, family, or circle of friends, boldly be the Lord’s witness. Not to exalt yourself, but to exalt the Lord who has abolished death, so that people see the eternal life he reveals.
q: What gifts or callings has God long placed in your heart that you have not used out of fear or by holding back? Are you willing today to fan into flame again the fire that comes from God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for placing a calling and gifts within me. I admit that at times I have held back out of fear, but today I want to fan into flame again the fire that comes from You. Give me a spirit of power, love, and self-control, so that I may boldly be Your witness and hold fast to the true way to the end. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Path of Mission Begins with Waiting
v: The first book I wrote, Theophilus, concerned all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
until the day in which he was received up, after he had given commandments through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen.
To them he also showed himself alive after his suffering by many proofs, appearing to them for forty days, and speaking the things concerning the Kingdom of God.
Being assembled together with them, he commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, “which”, said he, “you heard from me.
For John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now.”
Therefore, when they had come together, they asked him, “Lord, are you now restoring the Kingdom to Israel?”
He said to them, “It isn’t for you to know times or seasons which the Father has set within his own authority.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”
When he had said these things, as they were looking, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.
b: Before ascending to heaven, Jesus spent forty days with his disciples, showing them the reality of his resurrection and teaching them about the Kingdom of God. This time was not an ending but a turning point, the key moment of moving from “seeing the Lord walk with us” to “trusting the Lord’s guidance.”

The disciples were concerned about when the Kingdom would be restored to Israel, but Jesus drew their focus back to God’s sovereignty and plan, reminding them, “It isn’t for you to know.” What they were to do was wait for power from on high. This power was not for fulfilling personal dreams, but for completing the mission entrusted by God: to be his witnesses from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.

This is a path of faith, and also a selfless choice. No longer planning by ourselves, no longer relying on our own ability, but learning at each step to obey, look to him, and witness. Starting from waiting, our lives truly come into step with God’s rhythm and are ready for him to reign within us and show his glory through us.
a: Wait for God’s timing instead of rushing your own plans
Before important decisions, learn to be still and wait, because true power comes from God, not from our own impulses.
Return the authority of your life to God’s hands
It is not for me to arrange God’s actions, but to accept his guidance. Where my “Jerusalem” is and where my “ends of the earth” are, I leave to God to decide.
Start from where you are and live out your witness
Witness is not a slogan but a daily choice. Start at home, at work, and in church, and faithfully live out the role the Lord has entrusted to you.
q: Am I willing to begin with waiting, not relying on my own clever plans, but letting God lead my steps and accomplish his mission?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving a clear calling and an eternal hope. I am willing to wait for You and learn to hand authority back to You, so that my steps are no longer hasty and my plans no longer self-centered. May You Yourself guide me, and from today, starting right where I am, make me a faithful witness for You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When I Suffer, May Those Who Trust in You Not Be Put to Shame
v: Don’t let those who wait for you be shamed through me, Lord Yahweh of Armies. Don’t let those who seek you be brought to dishonor through me, God of Israel.
Because for your sake I have borne reproach. Shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother’s children.
For the zeal of your house consumes me. The reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me.
When I wept and chastened my soul with fasting, that was my reproach.
When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them.
Those who sit in the gate talk about me. I am the song of the drunkards.
But as for me, my prayer is to you, Yahweh, in an acceptable time. God, in the abundance of your loving kindness, answer me in the truth of your salvation.
Deliver me out of the mire, and don’t let me sink. Let me be delivered from those who hate me, and out of the deep waters.
Don’t let the flood waters overwhelm me, neither let the deep swallow me up. Don’t let the pit shut its mouth on me.
b: This is a psalm full of tears and faith. In extreme pain David prayed. He was misunderstood, mocked, and rejected; even his friends drew away, and his own kin regarded him as a stranger. But he did not fix his eyes on his own shame. He turned to God and said, “Don’t let those who wait for you be shamed through me.” This is a deeply God-centered response: even in suffering, putting God’s glory and the faith of others first.

David’s heart was deeply “consumed by zeal for God’s house,” and he suffered reproach for God, only to be mocked and ridiculed. This is similar to the situation we face today when our faith is challenged: in standing firm in faith and living out righteousness, we often bear pressure and misunderstanding from society, family, and even within the church. But it is in such circumstances that we can better practice handing authority back to God, and live out patience and perseverance by his loving kindness.

David’s final prayer was not an escape, but an honest request that God deliver him from the mire and the deep waters. He trusted that God’s loving kindness and faithfulness would in the end accomplish his purpose, so that all his suffering would not be in vain. He did not struggle free by himself, but looked wholeheartedly to God’s salvation. This is a way of life in which God is King and leads.
a: When you are misunderstood for your faith, learn like David to turn shame into prayer and trust in God.
In suffering, still care for the faith of others, and let your response help others trust in God.
When you meet difficulty, do not first ask for the circumstances to change, but ask God to give you a heart of strength, love, and self-control.
q: When I suffer and am shamed, am I willing to turn my eyes from myself to God? Can my response help others know God’s glory better?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, my heart is sorrowful in affliction, yet I look to You. Keep those who trust in You from being disappointed because of me, and do not let the enemy boast over me. Let my response glorify You and strengthen others, and in the right time, rescue me according to Your faithful loving kindness. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Set Aside Your Own Way and Return to God’s Word
v: Seek Yahweh while he may be found. Call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.
“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways,” says Yahweh.
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it bring forth and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater;
so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
b: When God says, “Seek Yahweh while he may be found,” it is not a cold command but a loving invitation. He longs for us to turn back, not because we are good enough, but because he delights to forgive and delights to draw near. Returning to God does not begin with outward behavior; it begins with turning the thoughts of our hearts toward his way.

God’s ways are higher than our ways, and his thoughts far above our thoughts. This reminds us that if we want to walk in his plan, we must set aside the logic we are comfortable with and the paths we are used to, and learn to surrender and look to him. God’s word is like rain and snow watering the earth: once it falls, it always bears fruit and never comes to nothing. When we choose to believe his word and follow his leading, even if our circumstances have not changed, something inside us has already begun to be transformed.

This is a “choice of selflessness”: laying down self-centered decisions, taking God’s heart as our measuring line, and living in the rhythm and faithfulness of his word. May we practice every day not leaning on our own understanding, but letting God’s way become a lamp to our feet and a light on our path.
a: Actively seek God’s heart, rather than relying only on your own thinking
In every decision, first ask, “How does God see this?” instead of “What makes the most sense to me?”
Courageously leave wrong ways of thinking and acting
When you notice thoughts and habits that don’t agree with God’s truth, adjust them right away. This is what true repentance looks like.
Let God’s word guide your steps every day
Don’t just read Scripture; let it enter your thinking and shape your choices, so that God’s word brings forth the fruit of life.
q: Am I willing to set aside my own ways and thoughts and truly turn back to God’s heart and leading?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for always stretching out Your loving hand and inviting me back into Your presence. Help me set aside my own judgments and plans, and learn to seek Your way in stillness. Let Your word keep watering my heart, so that I may bear the fruit of life in the purpose You have appointed. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Glory Belongs to God, Not to Show Off Ourselves
v: At that time, Berodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

Hezekiah listened to them, and showed them all the house of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, the precious oil, and the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah didn’t show them.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah, and said to him, “What did these men say? From where did they come to you?” Hezekiah said, “They have come from a far country, even from Babylon.”
He said, “What have they seen in your house?” Hezekiah answered, “They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them.”
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of Yahweh.
Behold, the days come that all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have laid up in store to this day, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,” says Yahweh.
“They will take away some of your sons who will issue from you, whom you will father; and they will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”
Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of Yahweh which you have spoken is good.” He said moreover, “Isn’t it so, if peace and truth will be in my days?”
b: After experiencing God’s wonderful healing, Hezekiah received envoys from Babylon. He could have used the moment to bear witness, to tell of Yahweh’s love and deliverance. Instead he chose to show off his treasures and his kingdom’s strength. In that moment his focus shifted from God to himself, from trust to display. As a result, God spoke through the prophet Isaiah: everything he had relied on would be carried away.

Hezekiah was a king who feared God, yet this passage reminds us that even a past of walking with God does not guarantee we will never drift from our focus. When we begin to treat God’s blessings as tools for achievement, when we long for people to praise our “treasures” rather than God’s works, we fall, like Hezekiah, into spiritual pride.

A truly godly life is a “choice of selflessness”: having much, yet not boasting; being rich, yet still fearing God; being honored, yet giving the glory to God. For everything we have was never meant to display ourselves, but to witness to God’s faithfulness and glory.
a: Remember that every blessing comes from God
In times of success and breakthrough, don’t only share the result; also bear witness to the grace and guidance of God behind it.
Leave the stage to God, and don’t build one for yourself
When people admire what you’ve accomplished, learn to turn their attention to God, rather than lingering on your own effort and ability.
Keep a reverent heart, and don’t be carried away by success
Spiritual heights without humility and vigilance can easily become a fatal weak point. May our hearts be set right again and again, never letting the glory rest on ourselves for long.
q: In my life, what are the gifts of God’s grace that I have carelessly turned into things to boast about?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for every grace and blessing You have given. I confess that sometimes I turn my focus to myself too quickly and forget that You are the source of everything. Keep me humble, so that all I have and all I experience may be a witness to You and bring You glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: For the Sake of the Gospel, I Gladly Lay Myself Down
v: For though I was free from all, I brought myself under bondage to all, that I might gain the more.
To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to those who are under the law, as under the law, though not being myself under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;
to those who are without law, as without law, not being without law toward God, but under the law of Christ, that I might win those who are without law.
To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.
Now I do this for the sake of the Good News, that I may be a joint partaker of it.
Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, that you may win.
Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
I therefore run like that, as not uncertainly. I fight like that, as not beating the air,
but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be disqualified.
b: This passage reveals the core attitude of a God-centered life: gladly setting aside one’s own rights for the Lord, so that more people may receive the gospel. Though Paul was free, he chose to become a servant to all kinds of people. This was not compromising the truth, but living out God’s love and wisdom, leading people to God with humility and consideration.

He reminds us that the spiritual life is like a race, and to win the crown that does not perish we need self-control and focus. A God-centered life is more than agreeing with a belief; it is choosing each day to let the Lord rule and to bring our conduct in line with his heart.

Finally, Paul closes with “I beat my body and bring it into submission,” showing that God’s people do not simply indulge themselves, but rely on the Holy Spirit to master the flesh and live a life of holiness and mission. We live not for ourselves, but for God’s glory and for the salvation of others.
a: In daily life, be willing to reach out to people of different backgrounds, learning to connect with them in love and wisdom and bring them to God.
Practice Bible reading, prayer, and self-control with discipline, training your spiritual life as a runner trains for a race.
Remind yourself every day
I do not live for myself, but so that Jesus may be known and honored.
q: Am I willing to adjust my way of life so others can know the gospel better? Do I care about my spiritual growth as seriously as an athlete preparing for competition?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me through Paul’s example that a life that truly belongs to You gladly sets itself aside and is willing to pay the price for the gospel. Help me learn self-control and discipline, and be willing to adapt and endure out of love, so that more people may come to know You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Draw Near to God with Gratitude and Reverence
v: Oh come, let’s sing to Yahweh. Let’s shout aloud to the rock of our salvation!
Let’s come before his presence with thanksgiving. Let’s extol him with songs!
For Yahweh is a great God, a great King above all gods.
In his hand are the deep places of the earth. The heights of the mountains are also his.
The sea is his, for he made it. His hands formed the dry land.
Oh come, let’s worship and bow down. Let’s kneel before Yahweh our Maker,
for he is our God. We are the people of his pasture, and the sheep in his hand. Today, if you will hear his voice,
b: This psalm opens with a warm invitation: “Oh come!” It calls us to draw near to God with singing, shouting, and thanksgiving. This is not a religious formality but the natural response of a life to its Creator. When we realize that God is the rock of our salvation, praise and thanks rise up from the heart.

The psalmist goes on to show that God’s greatness has no equal: he rules the deep places of the earth and the heights of the mountains, and he made the sea and the dry land. Everything is in his hands. Our lives are no accident; they come from his creation and care. So worship is not merely singing words, but an attitude of humbling ourselves and bowing down in reverence.

Finally, he reminds us that we are the sheep of God’s pasture, the people he has tended with his own hands. A God-centered life means no longer living for ourselves, but being willing to hear his voice and follow his lead. This is the practice of “letting God be King and giving God the glory,” and the expression of worship and trust from the inside out.
a: Begin each day with gratitude, worshiping God with songs or prayer, and don’t let circumstances rob you of praising him.
In the midst of busyness, learn to pause in reverence before God, acknowledging him as Creator, as your Shepherd and Lord.
When making decisions, learn to listen for God’s voice, relying not on your own judgment but letting God’s will guide you.
q: Do I worship God only out of habit? Am I willing to draw near to God sincerely, with reverence and gratitude, and listen to his word?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, I want to come to You with shouts of joy and thanksgiving, for You are the rock of my life and the shepherd of my soul. Teach me to have a heart of reverence and obedience, to listen to Your voice each day and follow Your lead. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Living with Faith in Eternity During Our Sojourn
v: Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years. This was the length of Sarah’s life.
Sarah died in Kiriath Arba (the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
Abraham rose up from before his dead, and spoke to the children of Heth, saying,
“I am a stranger and a foreigner living with you. Give me a possession of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
So the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all its borders, were deeded
to Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all who went in at the gate of his city.
After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan.
The field, and the cave that is in it, were deeded to Abraham by the children of Heth for a possession of a burying-place.
b: After Sarah’s death, Abraham faced not only personal grief but also a reminder of his standing in the land. He said, “I am a stranger and a foreigner.” Although God had long ago promised this land to him and his descendants, he still humbly bought land from the local people to bury his wife. This was not doubt about God’s word, but a deep faith: trusting God’s timing and God’s arrangement.

Abraham did not hurriedly bury Sarah just anywhere. He was willing to pay a price to obtain a piece of land that truly belonged to him. It was a declaration of faith: even though he had not yet fully received the promise, he was willing to prepare in the present and wait for the day it would be fulfilled. His choice bears witness to a man who deeply trusted God’s purpose and faithfulness, and who gladly lived in obedience and hope within limits.

This passage reminds us that our years on earth are only days of sojourning, yet in every sorrow, decision, and choice we can live out the values of God. Not by striving in the flesh, but by answering the call with our lives. Not by relying on comfortable circumstances, but by standing firm in our knowledge of God.
a: In loss and death, learn from Abraham to respond with faith, acting with respect and honesty.
View present choices with a long-term perspective and prepare for eternity; even if you don’t yet see the result, be willing to act faithfully.
In this world, don’t take yourself as the master, but live a life that knows its identity, submits to God’s authority, and trusts in God.
q: Do I often live as though this world is my permanent home? Am I willing, like Abraham, to show through every choice that I belong to God and trust in him?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, in this life of sojourning, teach me to trust Your word as Abraham did, not leaning on present comfort but making choices with eternal hope. In every loss and every decision, let me still honor You and obey You, until the day I see Your face. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Rich Generosity from Deep Poverty: Learning True Godliness from Joyful Giving
v: Moreover, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God which has been given in the churches of Macedonia;
how in much proof of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded to the riches of their liberality.
For according to their power, I testify, yes and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord,
begging us with much entreaty to receive this grace and the fellowship in the service to the saints.
This was not as we had hoped, but first they gave their own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.
So we urged Titus, that as he made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace.
But as you abound in everything—in faith, utterance, knowledge, all earnestness, and in your love to us—see that you also abound in this grace.
b: In this passage the apostle Paul particularly commends the example of the churches of Macedonia. Their situation was one of “deep poverty,” yet in great trial they had “abundance of joy,” and even in want they gave “beyond their power,” gladly and willingly. This did not come from human emotion but “through the will of God”: they first gave themselves to the Lord, and then took part in the act of giving. Their lives were not defined by circumstances but moved by grace.

This challenges us: giving does not wait until we have extra, but is possible whenever we are willing; it does not come from social pressure but from trust in God. True selflessness is not only letting go of material things, but the attitude of “first giving ourselves to the Lord.” When a person’s heart already belongs to God, laying down possessions is no longer hard.

If we want to grow in faith, knowledge, speech, and earnestness, Paul reminds us: “abound in this grace also.” Godliness does not stay in spiritual words; it must extend into action, using love to meet the needs of fellow believers and of God’s household.
a: Giving is not charity but part of worship
The Macedonian churches did not give because they were “wealthy,” but because they “gave themselves to the Lord.” Are you willing to let God use not just your money, but your whole self?
Practice selflessness in difficulty
Don’t wait until you have more resources before you start giving. Learn to trust God’s provision right now, and give God the first choice.
Live out your faith with genuine love
If you are truly growing in faith, knowledge, and love, express it in action: not just hearing the message, but doing it.
q: Am I willing, like the Macedonian churches, to give before I have plenty, to give myself to the Lord first and gladly share in the needs of God’s household?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the example of the Macedonian churches, which shows me what true selflessness and worship look like. Help me learn to offer myself fully to You, and not let my circumstances limit my trust in You or my response to You. May I also show faithfulness and love to You in acts of generosity. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When God Calls, Will You Answer?
v: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
Yahweh’s angel appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
Moses said, “I will go now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.”
When Yahweh saw that he came over to see, God called to him out of the midst of the bush, and said, “Moses, Moses!” He said, “Here I am.”
Yahweh said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters. I know their sorrows,

and I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
Come now therefore, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt.”
b: Moses had spent many years shepherding in the wilderness, and he assumed his life had already taken its final shape: far from the palace, far from passion, far from purpose. Yet on an ordinary day he met an extraordinary sign: a bush burning in the fire but not consumed. Through this vision God revealed himself to Moses and called his name: “Moses, Moses!” Moses answered, “Here I am.”

This was a life-changing call. God did not call Moses at the peak of his career, but spoke to him in the ordinary routine of his low point. This reminds us that God’s plan does not depend on our qualifications but on his timing. God not only “saw,” “heard,” and “knew” the suffering of his people; he “came down” to rescue them and “sent” someone to carry out his purpose.

God revealed his heart to Moses and invited him to take part in this great plan of redemption. It was a life change from “self” to “obedience”: no longer living in avoidance and comfort, but willing to answer God’s sending and step into the unknown, the challenge, and the mission.
a: Keep a sensitive heart to God’s call
Perhaps God is using something unusual in your everyday life to prompt you to respond. May our hearts, like Moses’, say, “Here I am.”
Don’t measure your destiny by your present situation
Moses had been in the wilderness for years and may have given up his earlier dreams, yet God called him then. What God values is not your past, but whether you are willing to obey now.
Let God’s plan rise above your own arrangements
Only when we are willing to set aside our own ideas and sense of security and respond to God’s sending do we truly step onto the path he has prepared for us.
q: When God calls me, am I willing, like Moses, to set aside my own way and obey his sending?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for seeing our suffering and for calling us to share in Your work of rescue. Help me have a sensitive heart, neither putting off nor fearing, and be willing to say, “Here I am,” when You call me. May You use my life to accomplish Your glorious purpose. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Remember the Lord Jesus and Live Out His Love and Mission
v: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.
When he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”
In the same way he also took the cup, after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in memory of me.”
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
b: The apostle Paul says, “For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you.” This is not merely a traditional saying but a sacred inheritance: Communion is not only a sign but a remembrance; not only a memory but an action.

On that dark night, the Lord Jesus broke the bread with his own hands, foretelling that he would give his body and shed his blood for our sins. He said, “Do this in memory of me.” This was not just a supper, but a covenant of love, a foreshadowing of the grace of the cross, and the beginning of the new covenant of the Kingdom of heaven.

Every time we eat the bread and drink the cup, it is a reminder to the soul: we are a redeemed people, a people in covenant with the Lord. This remembrance does not stay in ritual but extends into daily life: treating one another with love and looking to the Lord’s return with faith.
a: Let “remembering the Lord” be the center of every day
The Lord Jesus wants us to remember him not only at Communion, but to live out his likeness and love every day.
Respond to the Lord’s sacrifice and live out the new covenant life
His body was broken for us and his blood established the covenant; our lives too should be offered up as living sacrifices, living for him.
Welcome the Lord’s return with hope
Each Communion is a proclamation: the Lord has died for me, and he will surely come again for me. Let us prepare every day to meet him.⸻
q: Do I merely “attend Communion” without truly “remembering the Lord”? The Lord gave his life for me; am I also willing to live for him?
pr: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving Your body and shedding Your blood for me, and for establishing the new covenant with me. Help me not only take part in Communion outwardly, but truly remember You from the heart. May I live out Your love every day, wait for Your return, and never forget the grace You have accomplished for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Power of the Holy Spirit Comes Down and Reveals God’s Glory
v: Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place.
Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
Tongues like fire appeared to them and were distributed, and one sat on each of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.
Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men, from every nation under the sky.
When this sound was heard, the multitude came together, and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
They were all amazed and marveled, saying to one another, “Behold, aren’t all these who speak Galileans?
How do we hear, everyone in our own native language?
Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and the residents of Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia,
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, the parts of Libya around Cyrene, visitors from Rome, both Jews and proselytes,
Cretans and Arabians: we hear them speaking in our languages the mighty works of God!”
They were all amazed, and were perplexed, saying to one another, “What does this mean?”
b: On the day of Pentecost, the disciples were simply “all with one accord in one place,” never imagining that this gathering would become a turning point in history. Suddenly a sound like a mighty wind from heaven filled the whole house, and tongues like fire appeared and rested on each of them. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages.

This was not confusion but unity; not the scattered tongues of Babel, but the common speech of the Spirit. People of different nations and backgrounds all heard the disciples speaking “the mighty works of God” in their own languages!

This is the purpose of the Holy Spirit’s coming: not to make people show off spiritual experiences, but to lift high the glory of God; not to create a mysterious atmosphere, but to bear witness to Jesus and spread the gospel. This wind from heaven set ordinary people on fire and sent them boldly to every corner of the world to witness for the Lord.
a: Prepare your heart to welcome the work of the Holy Spirit

The disciples were gathered, but they were not idly waiting; they were praying continually and seeking him earnestly. We too should keep preparing our hearts to receive the renewing power of the Holy Spirit.
Let the Holy Spirit use us to proclaim God’s works
Being filled with the Spirit is not just for our own feelings, but so that we can speak of God’s deeds and make the Lord’s name known. You and I can become a “voice for the Kingdom of God.”
Believe that God will use us beyond our limits
Galileans spoke the languages of many nations; today God can also use us to speak a “language of the heart” that people can hear, opening hearts and leading them to the Lord.
q: Am I willing to be a vessel of the Holy Spirit? Am I willing to be filled with the Spirit, and let him use me to proclaim the mighty works of God?
pr: Dear Holy Spirit, I welcome You to fill me. Give me power, not to show off myself, but to proclaim the Lord’s glory and salvation. Use me beyond my weakness and limits, and make me a witness who pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When the World Sees Him Change You, They Will Honor His Name as Holy
v: “Therefore tell the house of Israel, ‘The Lord Yahweh says: “I don’t do this for your sake, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations, where you went.

I will sanctify my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you have profaned in the midst of them; and the nations will know that I am Yahweh,” says the Lord Yahweh, “when I will be sanctified in you before their eyes.
For I will take you from among the nations, and gather you out of all the countries, and will bring you into your own land.
I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your filthiness and from all your idols.
I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you will keep my ordinances and do them.
You will dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers. You will be my people, and I will be your God.”
b: Sometimes we think God’s blessings are a reward for us, but this passage makes it clear from the start: God restores his people not because they deserve it, but because he wants his own name to be honored as holy (36:22–23). When God’s people live unlike God’s people, even his name is treated lightly. Yet God still chooses to show grace, because his heart is that through our change the world would see his reality and glory.

God does not only want to change our circumstances; more importantly, he wants to change us completely on the inside. He says, “I will sprinkle clean water on you… I will give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will take away the stony heart… and give you a heart of flesh” (36:25–26). It is like someone going from cold to tender, from selfish to willing to give for others, from lost to back on the right path. Such change is not earned by our own effort but is the renewal brought by God’s Spirit living within.

When God’s Spirit works in our hearts, we begin to gladly obey his word, not out of fear but out of love; not by rules but because the nature of our life has changed (36:27). This is not only about knowing the faith but about living a life restored in relationship with God. He says, “You will be my people, and I will be your God” (36:28). This is a sense of security and identity that comes from being fully accepted and embraced again.
a: Let your life be a witness to God’s glory
Not by persuading the world with words, but by letting people see what God has done through a changed life.
Ask God to shine light on the parts of your heart that are still like stone
It may be a cold faith, defensiveness after being hurt, or the hardness of self-righteousness. Give it to God to renew.
Learn to obey the Holy Spirit’s prompting in small things
He does not ask us to become perfect, but to follow him step by step and experience true freedom and joy.
q: Does my life let people see God’s glory? Which parts of me am I willing to let God cleanse and change, so I may become a vessel for his glory?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for not giving up on me. Even though I have shamed Your name, You are still willing to change me so that Your name is glorified in me. Cleanse me and renew me, give me a new heart and a new spirit, so that I can live a life that pleases You. May my change let more people see You and know You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Don’t Let a Gullible Life Steal Your Spiritual Discernment
v: Stay away from a foolish man, for you won’t find knowledge on his lips.
The wisdom of the prudent is to think about his way, but the folly of fools is deceit.
The backslider in heart gets filled with his own ways; likewise a good man is filled with the fruit of his ways.
A simple man believes everything, but the prudent carefully considers his steps.
b: In this age of information overload and clamoring voices, the ability to tell true from false and right from wrong has become a key spiritual skill. Proverbs reminds us: “Stay away from a foolish man, for you won’t find knowledge on his lips” (14:7). Some people speak very persuasively but have no foundation in truth; their words may be clever yet without wisdom, even a deceit that deceives themselves (14:8).

By contrast, the “prudent” are not those who know everything, but those who “think about [their] way.” They do not simply follow the crowd, a person, or a trend; they are willing to quiet down and ask themselves, “Is the way I’m going right? Is it from God?” This knowledge of one’s own path is wisdom from God and the mark of a life lived in the light.

When a person believes every voice, in the end he will be overwhelmed by confusion. Scripture says, “A simple man believes everything, but the prudent carefully considers his steps” (14:15). Faith is not blindness, nor an emotional impulse, but a firm choice made after spiritual discernment.

The outcomes are also completely different: “The backslider in heart gets filled with his own ways; likewise a good man is filled with the fruit of his ways” (14:14). God lets everyone eat the fruit of what they have sown, but to those who choose the way of goodness and uprightness, he promises a satisfaction and peace that come from within.
a: Learn to discern the voices you listen to
Not every teaching agrees with the truth, and not every word is worth believing. Let God’s word be the filter for your thinking.
Form the habit of examining your own path
Don’t only check whether others are right; often ask yourself, “Is the way I think and walk in line with God’s heart?”
When unsure, slow down and take each step carefully
The prudent are not the fastest runners, but those whose every step is in God’s guidance.
q: Do I often believe what people say and decide rashly? Am I willing to let God’s word adjust me so that I live with more wisdom and discernment?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, grant me spiritual discernment, so that I will not be a simple person who believes every voice. Teach me to understand my own path, to walk in the light, and to accept the guidance and pruning of Your word. Make me careful in every step, walking on the right path You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: The Earthly Tent Will Be Destroyed; Our Heavenly Home Will Never Be Shaken
v: For we know that if the earthly house of our tent is destroyed, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.
For most assuredly in this we groan, longing to be clothed with our habitation which is from heaven,
if so be that being clothed we will not be found naked.
For indeed we who are in this tent do groan, being burdened, not that we desire to be unclothed, but that we desire to be clothed, that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
Now he who made us for this very thing is God, who also gave to us the down payment of the Spirit.
Being therefore always of good courage, and knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord;
for we walk by faith, not by sight.
We are of good courage, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body and to be at home with the Lord.
Therefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well pleasing to him.
For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
b: Every day we live in a “tent”, a body that grows tired, gets hurt, and ages. Paul says we know that this tent will one day be taken down, but we also have assurance: God has prepared another home for us that will never be destroyed, not a house on earth, but an eternal house in the heavens (5:1).

In this life we inevitably groan and labor (5:2, 5:4), but this is not despair; it is longing. Like someone waiting at an airport, tired yet full of anticipation, what we long for deep inside is not merely to escape, but to be “clothed” with that heavenly life, so that we are no longer naked, that is, no longer ashamed, empty, or adrift.

God has put the Holy Spirit within us as the “down payment” of all these promises, a deposit guaranteeing that what he has said will be accomplished (5:5). So we can face all of life’s uncertainties with good courage, because we do not live by feelings or sight, but by faith, in hope (5:6–7).

In the end, our aim is not success or being affirmed, but “to be well pleasing to him,” because one day we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ and receive his evaluation (5:9–10). This is not a fearful judgment, but the true value and direction of life.
a: Value the inner life more than the outer tent
The body will break down and circumstances will change, but what God builds within you is eternal and unshakable.
In pain and toil, learn to replace complaining with hope
Groaning is a process, not the end. God will swallow up death with life and replace decay with glory.
Live to please God, preparing to meet the Lord face to face
Every choice and every day is preparation for that meeting.
q: Am I living with an eternal perspective? When facing physical decline or a low point in life, do I still believe that God has prepared a better home for me?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for preparing a heavenly home for me that will never be destroyed. When I groan in this life, make Your promises more real to me. Give me faith to live each day in a way that pleases You, ready for the day I meet You face to face. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Worship God with Your Life and Live in a Way That Pleases Him
v: Through him, then, let us offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips which proclaim his name.
But don’t forget to be doing good and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

Obey your leaders, and submit to them, for they watch on behalf of your souls, as those who will give account, that they may do this with joy, and not with groaning, for that would be unprofitable for you.
Pray for us, for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, desiring to live honorably in all things.
I strongly urge you to do this, that I may be restored to you sooner.
Now the God of peace, who brought again from the dead the great Shepherd of the sheep with the blood of the eternal covenant, even our Lord Jesus,
make you complete in every good work to do his will, working in us that which is well pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
b: When we think of worship, we often think of songs, prayers, or Sunday gatherings. But Hebrews reminds us that true worship is “through him,” offering praise to God as a sacrifice (13:15). It is not a momentary feeling but a “continual” thanksgiving and praise from the heart, the expression of a life that acknowledges Jesus as Lord and is willing to honor his name.

Yet worship is not only on the lips; it must also show in action. “Don’t forget to be doing good and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased” (13:16). In a self-centered, calculating world, a heart willing to think of others and gladly share is the truest worship.

Our faith should not be a solo effort either. God has appointed spiritual leaders who “watch on behalf of your souls, as those who will give account” (13:17). When we are willing to submit to authority and pray for one another, God can build unity and joy in the church.

The closing blessing is deeply moving: may God “make you complete in every good work to do his will, working in us that which is well pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ” (13:21). The goal of faith is not only to receive help, but to become people who please God, living out his heart and glory.
a: Turn praise into a habit, letting worship extend into every part of life
In good times and bad, lips that continually magnify the Lord are the very breath of God’s children.
Worship God with practical action
When you do good, share, and care for those in need, you are offering the sacrifice God accepts.
Submit to spiritual authority and walk together in mutual prayer
God uses pastors and spiritual companions to guide us, and supporting one another makes the whole body more joyful and strong.
q: Do I limit worship to singing and gatherings? In what parts of my life can I offer a “sacrifice” that pleases God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for letting me come before You boldly to worship through Jesus. May my worship be more than words, but a true witness in my life. Help me praise You continually, and live out Your likeness in doing good and in love. May You be pleased with my imperfect life, and accomplish Your perfect purpose. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Cast Your Anxieties on God and Stand Firm in Faith
v: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time;
casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.
But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, make you perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
To him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
b: Facing great pressure and trouble in life, we often ask, “Lord, when will I be free from these worries?” But Peter points out that the breakthrough begins not with gritting our teeth on our own, but with “humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God” (5:6). This is not putting ourselves down; it is choosing to trust the all-knowing, almighty God. When we choose to lay ourselves down, God will, at the right time, lift us to a higher place.

Such trust needs real action: “casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you” (5:7). It is not praying once and then taking the worry back, nor worrying while praying, but choosing every day to put our anxiety, pressure, and difficulty into God’s hands. For he is not a distant God; he cares about every tear and every heartbeat.

Peter also reminds us that on this road of faith, the enemy is not just the problems, but the devil who “walks around like a roaring lion” (5:8). He wants to use your fear, doubt, and weariness to devour you. But we do not fight alone, for brothers and sisters all over the world face the same struggles (5:9), and we have firm faith and the Lord’s grace walking with us.

Finally, Peter brings the firmest promise: suffering is not forever, and the God of grace will “himself” make you perfect, establish you, and strengthen you (5:10). You are not abandoned; you are being equipped. You are not going to fall; you are being lifted up by God’s own hands.
a: Practice truly handing your anxieties to God
Not just saying a prayer, but each time anxiety strikes, choosing to entrust it and let go.
Stay alert and watch for gaps in your soul
Temptation often starts in small places we overlook. Keep yourself within God’s word and the protection of companions.
Build a strong network of faith and don’t face spiritual battle alone
Walking together and praying for one another is an important line of defense against the enemy.
q: Do I tend to bottle up pressure rather than give it to God? Am I willing to stand firm in the spiritual battle and trust the Lord who personally strengthens me?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, I choose to humble myself and cast all my anxieties on You, because You care for me. Keep me alert so that the enemy cannot devour me, and help me rely firmly on You in faith. Even in suffering, I believe You will personally perfect me and give me strength. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: You Are No Longer a Slave, but a Child of God
v: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God;
and if children, then heirs: heirs of God, and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.
b: In a world of fierce competition and constant comparison, we often fall into a slave mentality: Am I good enough? Do I perform well enough to be loved? Will I be rejected or cast out? But God tells us clearly through Paul: you are not a slave, you are a child of God.

“For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God” (8:14). Faith is not about earning qualification through works; it is about being led by the Holy Spirit and building an intimate relationship with God. It is not because you have done enough, but because you belong to him, and he lives in you and guides your every step.

Paul says, “You didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear… but you received the Spirit of adoption” (8:15). In Christ we can cry out boldly and without fear, “Abba! Father!” This is not a cold religious title, but the most natural, intimate cry of a child to a father. We are not servants working for God; we are children living in his house.

Even more precious, we are not only children but heirs, sharing God’s inheritance with Christ (8:17): not only the glory of heaven, but also his presence, love, strength, and mission that he wants to give right now. The road of following the Lord may bring suffering, but our hope will surely be glory.
a: Change how you know God: he is not a harsh master but a loving Father
Your relationship with God is not won by performance but received by faith. Learn to rest in his love.
Learn to be led by the Holy Spirit in daily life
The identity of a child lets us hear his voice and sense his guidance, rather than deciding everything ourselves.
Accept your identity as an heir and courageously take up the mission of the Kingdom
God does not only want to bless you; he wants to use you. You are not a supporting character, but a part of the Kingdom’s plan.
q: Am I still living my faith with a slave’s heart? Do I truly believe that I am a beloved child of God, who will share in Christ’s glory?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for accepting me as Your child through Jesus. Take away the fear and doubt of a slave within me, and let me cry to You in love, “Abba, Father!” Lead me by Your Spirit every day, that I may live out my identity as Your child, suffering with Christ and being glorified with him. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: God Does Not Forget You, and He Blots Out All Your Transgressions
v: “Remember these things, Jacob, and Israel, for you are my servant. I have formed you. You are my servant. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.
I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.”
