Sing, you heavens, for Yahweh has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, and every tree in it, for Yahweh has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.
Thus says Yahweh, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb: “I am Yahweh, who makes all things; who stretches forth the heavens alone; who spreads abroad the earth by myself;
who frustrates the signs of the liars, and makes diviners mad; who turns wise men backward, and makes their knowledge foolish;
b: In relationships, being forgotten is heartbreaking. But God says to his people, “I have formed you… you will not be forgotten by me” (44:21). Even when we keep being weak, stumbling, and even drifting from him, God does not give up on us, because we are the work of his hands, servants in his eyes, treasures in his heart.

He goes further and declares: “I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins” (44:22). Our sins are not merely covered or overlooked; they are completely wiped away, like clouds clearing from a bright sky without a trace. God does not accept us because we have no sin; he first redeemed us so that we could return to him.

This is not only a personal grace but something the whole universe should celebrate (44:23). God’s salvation does not happen quietly; it calls heaven, earth, mountains, and trees to praise together. For his glory is revealed not only in nature, but in a lost soul found and a broken heart restored.

He is the God who has known you since you were formed in the womb (44:24). He created the heavens and the earth and acts on his own; he brings the pretensions of men to nothing (44:25). But to you, who are willing to turn back, he will never say, “It’s too late.”
a: Remind yourself every day
God has not forgotten you. When you feel lonely and overlooked, he still remembers you, loves you, and calls you.
Accept God’s forgiveness and stop living in the shadow of your transgressions
You are not your past, nor the mistakes you have made. You are redeemed by God, blotted clean.
Return your life to the Lord who made you
He not only created you, but knows how to restore you. Don’t walk through life in your own way; return to his hands.
q: Do I believe that God truly does not forget me? Am I willing to let go of self-blame and shame and receive his complete forgiveness?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for never forgetting me. Even though I am weak and have failed, You blot out all my transgressions. I want to return to You and give You my life, and let You reign in my heart again. May my life become a witness to Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: With Unveiled Face Beholding the Lord’s Glory, Your Life Will Be Changed
v: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,
and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face, so that the children of Israel would not look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.
But their minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.
But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.
But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
But we all, with unveiled face reflecting as a mirror the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.
b: Many people read the Bible and listen to sermons yet feel no presence of God and no change. This is not because God’s glory is not bright enough, but because there is still a “veil” over the heart: doubt, pride, self-centeredness, religious habit. These veils keep us from seeing God’s true face and from truly drawing near to him.

Paul reminds us that in Christ this veil has been taken away (3:14). **When we are willing to “turn to the Lord,” the veil is removed from our hearts, and light can come in.** This is not a breakthrough in knowledge but a turning in relationship. It is not knowing the Bible better, but longing more to meet the Lord.

“Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty” (3:17). This freedom is not only freedom from the burden of the law, but freedom to draw near to God, freedom to be changed by him, and freedom to live as our true selves. We no longer need to hide; we can come with “unveiled face” to behold the Lord’s glory.

This beholding is not a one-time event but a lifelong journey: “transformed into the same image from glory to glory” (3:18). True change does not come from pressure or from self-discipline, but “from the Lord, the Spirit.” The Holy Spirit shapes us a little more each day, making us more and more like Jesus.
a: Practice coming before God with “unveiled face” every day
You don’t have to be perfect to meet God; come with your honesty and weakness, and let the Lord’s glory change you personally.
Remove the veil from your heart and stop viewing life by yourself
Relying on knowledge, experience, or other people’s opinions will only blur your focus. Turn to the Lord and he will shine his light on you personally.
Believe that the Holy Spirit is at work within you
Don’t be discouraged by your shortcomings; God is leading you from one glory to another.⸻
q: Am I still wearing some “veils” that keep me from truly meeting God? Am I willing to let the Holy Spirit renew me every day to make me more like Jesus?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, I want to remove every covering from my heart and open myself before You. Let me see Your glory, and let me be changed by Your Spirit, becoming more and more like Jesus from the inside out. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Come to God and Find True Satisfaction and Joy
v: “Hey, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
Why do you spend money for that which is not bread? and your labor for that which doesn’t satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.
Turn your ear, and come to me; hear, and your soul will live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways,” says Yahweh.
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it bring forth and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater;
so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
For you will go out with joy, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.
Instead of the thorn will come up the cypress tree; and instead of the brier will come up the myrtle tree: and it will make a name for Yahweh, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.”
b: In this busy and empty world, God sends an invitation to every “thirsty” soul: “Come to the waters!” (55:1). You don’t need to prepare anything, and you don’t need money to deserve it. God says, “Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.” This is the call of grace, the love of the Heavenly Father inviting you home.

Many people pour their energy, time, and money into things that “don’t satisfy” (55:2): pursuing surface success, fleeting pleasure, and approval from others. But God says: come and listen to me, come near to me, and you will eat what is truly good and receive the joy and peace that well up from within.

When we humbly listen to God’s word, we come to understand that his thoughts and ways are far beyond our imagination (55:8–9). We may not fully understand his arrangements, but we can fully trust his faithfulness and wisdom.

Just as rain and snow water the earth and never return empty, God’s word never comes to nothing (55:10–11). When his word reaches us and enters our lives, it brings transformation and growth, letting a barren heart grow cypress and myrtle (55:13) in place of thorns and briers. God’s word will change our lives and make us a witness to his glory.
a: Stop, and respond to God’s invitation
Stop wearing yourself out on things that cannot truly satisfy you. Are you thirsty? Then come to God.
Put your faith in God’s thoughts and ways
Not understanding does not mean God is wrong. Learn to trust that his way is always best.
Let God’s word water your parched heart every day
Like rain on the soil, God’s word will make you bear the fruit of faith, hope, and love.
q: Am I toiling for things that cannot truly feed my soul? Am I willing to let God’s word become the food of my life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, I want to stop and come into Your presence. Keep me from seeking what cannot truly satisfy, and make me hunger for Your word. Let Your word water my life so that I find true peace and joy. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Grace Renews Us, and Doing Good Benefits Others
v: Remind them to be in subjection to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
to speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.
For we were also once foolish ourselves, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,
not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,
whom he poured out on us richly, through Jesus Christ our Savior;
that being justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

This saying is faithful, and concerning these things I desire that you affirm confidently, so that those who have believed God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable to men;
but shun foolish questionings, genealogies, strife, and disputes about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.
Reject a factious man after a first and second warning;
knowing that such a one is perverted, and sins, being self-condemned.
b: This passage reminds us that Christians are saved not only to go to heaven, but to live a life that matches the gospel. We learn to submit to authority, respect order, actively do good, live at peace with others, and treat people gently. For we too were once in darkness, lost, rebellious, and quarrelsome, living in envy and hatred (3:1–3), but God did not treat us according to our deeds; he saved us by his kindness and love.

This grace is not something we traded for or earned, but comes “through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit” (3:5), so that change begins within us, from old self to new self. God not only forgave our sins but gave the power and life of the Holy Spirit, making us heirs with the hope of eternal life (3:7).

So true faith will surely lead to action. We are not saved in order to do good; we do good because we are saved (3:8). Doing good is not to win praise but to glorify God and build up others. As for those who only argue and refuse to change, Paul says to warn them, and if they will not repent, to turn away from them, so that we do not fall into vain and unprofitable quarrels (3:9–11).
a: Let grace change your words and conduct
What you used to be does not matter; what matters is whether you are willing to let God change you now and live a new life.
Witness to your faith through good works, and avoid fruitless arguments
The world will not come to know God because you win a debate, but it will sense the true light of the Lord through the love and honesty you live out.
Ask the Holy Spirit to renew your heart and spirit every day
Christians do not become better by their own effort; they are poured out upon, pruned, and shaped by the Holy Spirit day by day.
q: Am I willing to let God’s grace go beyond faith knowledge and truly shape my way of life? Do I take care to do good and live in a way that pleases God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for saving me by grace, not by what I have done but by Your love. Renew me by the Holy Spirit every day, so that I no longer live in the patterns of the past, but live as Your child, careful to do good and glorify Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: You Have a New Identity in Christ and Share in the Inheritance
v: For you are all children of God, through faith in Christ Jesus.
For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
If you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to promise.
b: This passage proclaims a most beautiful truth to us: through faith we are no longer merely created beings, but are called “children” by God, with an intimate relationship, a noble identity, and an eternal inheritance.

When we are baptized into Christ, we have “put on Christ” (3:27). This is not merely an outward ritual but an inward turning of life, like putting on a new garment: from then on, we no longer see our past and failures, but see Christ’s righteousness, beauty, and new life.

And in Christ all barriers are torn down: there is no distinction of race, status, or gender (3:28). We relate to God not through birth, achievement, or position, but by faith alone, becoming one with all who are in Christ, a new family.

Even more wonderful, since we belong to Christ, we are linked to God’s promise to Abraham and become heirs of what God promised (3:29). This inheritance includes his presence and guidance in this life, and eternal glory and the Kingdom. It is not only a hope for the future, but an identity and power we can experience today.
a: Accept your true identity in Christ
You are not here by accident, nor are you less than others. You are a child of God, with a glorious calling and destiny.
Live out unity in Christ in your relationships
Don’t let background or differences become barriers; accept one another with Christ’s love and belong to one another.
Declare every day that God’s promises are yours
Don’t live in lack and self-denial, for you are an heir, and God’s abundance will be revealed in your life.
q: Do I truly believe I am a child of God? Am I willing to let go of inferiority and barriers, and live out the unity and dignity that are mine in Christ?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for making me Your child through Jesus. I want to accept this new identity, put on Christ, and live out the beauty You have given. Help me show unity and love in my relationships, and live each day in the abundance of Your promises. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: No More Worry, Because My Heavenly Father Cares for Me
v: “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.”
b: In these words Jesus gently reminds us that worry changes nothing; it only steals our peace. He is not telling us to dodge our responsibilities. He is inviting us to look at life with new eyes: the Father’s heart as our standard, Jesus’ trust as our example, and the Holy Spirit’s leading as our support. This is the way of life that turns toward God.

He says, “Your heavenly Father knows.” What intimate comfort! He is not a distant ruler but a Father who watches over us with tender care. If the birds and the wildflowers are provided for, how much more the children he bought back at such a great price? When we shift our focus from material things to the Kingdom of heaven, we discover that real abundance in life is not about what we gain, but about who walks with us.

So Jesus says, “Seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness.” This is not just a spiritual slogan; it is a reordering of life. Let Jesus be King in our hearts, let God’s will be the standard for our daily decisions, and let the Holy Spirit guide us in our worries and turn us toward trust and rest.
a: Each morning, hand your worries over to your heavenly Father
Learn to be still before the Lord, give today’s burdens to him, and trust that he cares for all your needs.
Put seeking God’s heart first in every choice
Don’t start by asking, “Is this good for me?” Ask instead, “Does this please God?”
Trusting instead of fretting is your daily decision
Worry cannot solve problems, but trust can lead you out of the darkness and into the assurance of peace.
q: Is there a worry in my heart that I have been unwilling to give to God? Am I willing to start today to learn to seek first his Kingdom and his righteousness?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, I admit that I often worry because of the pressures of life, but You are the Lord who knows everything I need. Today I am willing to place all of it in Your hands. Help me to seek Your Kingdom and Your righteousness first every day. Let Jesus be King in my heart, and let the Holy Spirit lead me along the path of trust. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Place What You Have in the Lord’s Hands and See a Miracle
v: Jesus therefore lifting up his eyes, and seeing that a great multitude was coming to him, said to Philip, “Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?”
This he said to test him, for he himself knew what he would do.
Philip answered him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may receive a little.”
One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,
“There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?”
Jesus said, “Have the people sit down.” Now there was much grass in that place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
Jesus took the loaves; and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down; likewise also of the fish as much as they desired.
When they were filled, he said to his disciples, “Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, that nothing be lost.”
So they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which were left over by those who had eaten.
When therefore the people saw the sign which Jesus did, they said, “This is truly the prophet who comes into the world.”
Jesus therefore, perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force, to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself.
b: In this passage we see Jesus facing the hunger of five thousand people. He is not anxious, and he is not in a hurry to prove his power. With calm eyes he sees an opportunity to test faith. He asks Philip, “Where are we to buy bread?” but in fact he himself “knew what he would do” (6:6). God is never short of answers; he is looking to see whether we will respond to his work with faith.

The disciples calculated with realism and reason: “Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient.” But the boy responded with simple giving: “Here are five loaves and two fish.” From a human point of view, what are these “among so many”? Yet in the Lord’s hands, if we are willing to lay it down, even something small can become the starting point of a miracle.

Jesus did not complain that the resources were few, and he did not blame anyone for not helping. He did just one thing: he “gave thanks” and gave it out (6:11). This is a pattern for our lives: **don’t look first at how much you have; first give thanks, then entrust it, then share it.** In the end the crowd was not only filled, but twelve baskets were left over, showing that God’s provision is abundant and more than enough.

The ending is also worth pondering. When the crowd, excited by the miracle, wanted to take Jesus by force and make him king, he withdrew to the mountain (6:15). Someone who truly lets God be King does not use God to carry out their own plans, but submits to God’s will and God’s timing.
a: Give your “five loaves and two fish” to the Lord
You may feel insignificant, but when you lay it down, God can use it to bless many people.
When you face a need, give thanks first, then entrust it
Don’t wait until you have enough resources to act. Thank God and trust him first, and he will open the way.
Submit to God’s plan and don’t take God for your own use
Don’t merely expect God to carry out your arrangements. Let Jesus be King and lead you into his purpose.
q: Am I holding back because of my “not enough”? Am I willing to give what little I have to God, and let him use it to do more than I ask or imagine?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for being the One who supplies abundantly. Even though what I have is limited, when it is placed in Your hands it can become the beginning of a miracle. Help me to stop looking at my lack and to see Your faithfulness. May I be willing every day to lay down, give thanks, and share, and become a channel of Your blessing. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: When You Call Out, God Rescues You Himself
v: I love you, Yahweh, my strength.
Yahweh is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower.
He sent from on high, and he took me. He drew me out of many waters.
He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me; for they were too mighty for me.
They came on me in the day of my calamity, but Yahweh was my support.
He also brought me out into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
b: In this psalm David uses deeply affectionate words to express his trust in God and his gratitude. He does not begin with miracles; he begins with the heart: “I love you, Yahweh, my strength” (18:1). This is a life that turns its focus to God, letting him be Lord, no longer relying on self but depending on his strength alone.

In his trouble David cried out, and God reached down from on high and himself pulled him out of the great waters (18:16). David did not boast of clever escapes or brag about his courage. He admitted, “They were too mighty for me… but Yahweh was my support.” This is humility: admitting our own limits and taking refuge completely in the rock of God that cannot be shaken.

God not only rescued him, he “brought me out into a large place,” giving him freedom, room to breathe, and hope, “because he delighted in me” (18:19). These words are stunning. It is not that we are so great; it is that God delights in us by his grace. When we submit to the Holy Spirit’s leading and let God rule, our trouble is no longer a dead end but the beginning of a story of grace.
a: Under pressure, turn your focus from the problem back to God
Like David, begin your prayer with “I love you,” and let God’s presence replace the voice of fear.
Don’t rely on yourself or fear strong enemies; depend wholeheartedly on God
When enemies seem stronger than you and circumstances bigger than you, that is the very moment to experience God’s power.
Believe that God will lead you out into a wide-open place
He does not merely give you a hand up; he wants to bring you into the promise of freedom, joy, and glory.
q: In my troubles, do I still believe that God’s help is on its way? Am I willing to lay down my own struggling and depend on his salvation and strength alone?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, You are my rock, my shield, and my high tower. When I have no strength, You are my support; in my trouble, You reach down and rescue me Yourself. Thank You for saving me because You delight in me. May I spend my whole life in the wide-open place You have opened for me, living out Your glorious purpose. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Fix Your Eyes on Jesus and Run the Whole Race Without Losing Heart
v: Therefore let us also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.
b: On our spiritual journey, we do not go forward alone. We are surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses of faith who cheer us on. Their lives tell us that even when circumstances are hard, if we do not give up trusting, we can complete the road the Lord has entrusted to us.

But to run this heavenly race, we must first “lay aside” and “throw off.” We lay aside the unnecessary weights, such as excessive self-blame, other people’s expectations, and past wounds. We also throw off the sins that so easily entangle us, such as pride, self-righteousness, doubt, and bitterness. This letting go is not done by willpower, but by the power of letting Jesus be King and being led by the Holy Spirit.

We do not press on in our own strength, but “look to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith” (12:2). He is our example and also our source of strength. For the joy set before him, Jesus endured the shame of the cross. When we think of how he too was misunderstood, rejected, and attacked, yet remained faithful to the end, we find courage in our hearts to keep running and not grow weary or lose heart (12:3).
a: Examine yourself daily
Am I carrying burdens God never asked me to carry? Learn to set them down, not relying on yourself, but handing them to the Father’s hands.
Take the initiative to deal with the sins and weaknesses that entangle you
The Holy Spirit will shine his light on us and help us break free from the hidden problems that seem small but hinder our running.
Turn your eyes from yourself to Jesus
Don’t look only at circumstances and feelings. Look in faith to the Lord who has already won the victory and reigns.
q: What are the “weights” and “entanglements” in my life right now? Am I willing to turn my eyes to Jesus and rely on him to complete my life’s mission?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for opening a new and living way through Jesus. Help me to lay down my burdens and break free from the bonds of sin, so that I may fix my eyes on Jesus and, by the strength he gives, run with perseverance the race You have prepared for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: God Shepherds His People Himself and Raises Up a Righteous King
v: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” says Yahweh.

Therefore Yahweh, the God of Israel, says against the shepherds who feed my people: “You have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them. Behold, I will visit on you the evil of your doings,” says Yahweh.
“I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all the countries where I have driven them, and will bring them again to their folds; and they will be fruitful and multiply.
I will set up shepherds over them who will feed them. They will fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither will any be lacking,” says Yahweh.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will raise to David a righteous Branch, and he will reign as king and deal wisely, and will execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell safely. This is his name by which he will be called: Yahweh our righteousness.”
“Therefore behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that they will no more say, ‘As Yahweh lives, who brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;’

but, ‘As Yahweh lives, who brought up and who led the offspring of the house of Israel out of the north country, and from all the countries where I had driven them.’ They will dwell in their own land.”
b: In the time of the prophet Jeremiah, many spiritual leaders failed the trust God had given them. Instead of caring for the flock, they harmed and scattered it (23:1–2). God would not let this go on. He declared that he himself would step in, personally seek out his sheep, and raise up true shepherds to watch over them (23:3–4). This reminds us that God’s people are not any person’s property; they are a flock that God himself shepherds and cares for.

In the end, God’s promise centers on one key figure: “I will raise to David a righteous Branch,” who is Jesus Christ (23:5). He is the true King who acts with wisdom and carries out justice and righteousness. He does not rule according to human expectations, but shepherds according to the Father’s will.

This King’s name is “Yahweh our righteousness.” He does not merely act righteously; he himself is our righteousness (23:6). When we let Jesus be King, are led by the Holy Spirit along his path, and take the Bible as the standard for how we live, we can dwell in safety amid chaos and upheaval, like sheep finding peace in the hands of a good shepherd.
a: Don’t rely on human authority; trust in Jesus alone, the righteous King
Even when the leaders of this world fail, God still reigns, and he will prepare true shepherds and a true path for you.
Obey Jesus’ leading and live in his righteousness
Don’t try to be made righteous by works. We are counted righteous by faith, so let his life be the foundation of how you live each day.
Become a shepherd or spiritual leader after God’s own heart
If you serve others, do it not for your own gain, but to reflect the heart of the Great Shepherd and lead people toward the way of life.
q: In my life, is Jesus truly the King I follow? Do I let his righteousness be the measure of my actions?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not leaving us scattered and lost, but for seeking and gathering us Yourself. Thank You for raising up Jesus Christ as our righteous King and Shepherd. I want to follow him alone, trust him, obey him, and dwell in safety under his leading. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: In a Crisis, Fear God and Wait for His Revelation
v: In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep went from him.
Then the king commanded to call the magicians, and the enchanters, and the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king.
The king said to them, “I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.”
Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Syriac, “King, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will show the interpretation.”
The king answered the Chaldeans, “The thing is gone from me. If you don’t make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut in pieces, and your houses will be made a dunghill.
The decree went out, and the wise men were to be slain; and they sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.
Then Daniel returned answer with prudence and discretion to Arioch the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon;
he asked Arioch the king’s captain, “Why is the decree so urgent from the king?” Then Arioch made the thing known to Daniel.
Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the king the interpretation.
Then Daniel went to his house, and made the thing known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions,
that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret, that Daniel and his companions should not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
b: When human wisdom and strength fail, that is the time to fear God and wait for his revelation. King Nebuchadnezzar was deeply disturbed by a strange dream. He ordered all his magicians not only to interpret the dream but to tell him what it was, on pain of death (2:5). This extreme crisis showed that everything people rely on had gone bankrupt. Only the God of heaven can reveal mysteries that the human heart cannot grasp.

Daniel faced this challenge of life and death without panic, and without relying on his own cleverness. He chose first to answer the captain of the king’s guard with discretion (2:14), and then asked for time so he could seek God’s will (2:16). He went back to his companions in faith, and together they prayed, looking to the God who rules history to show mercy (2:17–18).

This passage shows us: **the fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom; relying on his law and revelation is the road to understanding.** Daniel did not lean on foreign learning or on his own brightness. He placed himself in God’s hands and waited for the Most High to instruct him. When God revealed the secret to him in a night vision (2:19), Daniel did not boast of his ability, but immediately praised the God who gives wisdom and light.
a: In an emergency, learn to fear God rather than rush to fix things
Like Daniel, step back and be still before God and seek his guidance, instead of hurriedly relying on your own experience.
Build a circle of faith companions who walk with God
Daniel did not pray alone; he sought the Lord with companions who feared God. This reminds us that in hard times, a God-centered fellowship is a source of strength.
Give the glory to God, remembering that all wisdom and revelation come from him
God reveals things to us not to promote us but to carry out his plan and display his glory.
q: When I face a difficulty, do I seek God first, or lean on my own methods? Do I believe that God is glad to reveal his heart to those who fear him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, in confusion and crisis I admit my limits and helplessness. Thank You that You are the God who shows mercy and reveals mysteries. Give me a heart of reverence, so that I will not lean on myself but wait for Your guidance. Let me also seek You together with those who love You, and walk the right path You have prepared for me. May all the wisdom and light I receive be for the glory of Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Let Drawing Near to God Be the Start of Every Day
v: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.
Simon and those who were with him followed after him;
and they found him, and said to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
He said to them, “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”
He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.
b: In just a few verses we see a crucial habit in the life of Jesus: drawing near to the Father early in the morning and seeking his will. Even at the height of his ministry, when “everyone is looking for you,” he still chose to rise early, leave the crowd, and pray in a deserted place (1:35). This was not escape but foundation; not passivity but respect for the Father’s authority and obedience to him.

Jesus’ reply is worth thinking about: “Let’s go elsewhere… because I came out for this reason” (1:38). He did not let people’s expectations decide his direction. His actions did not follow applause; they followed his sending. This is our example: let God rule each day, and let his will be the standard for how we move forward.

This is also how we put faith into practice: not by busyness alone, but by being still first; not by first asking what people want, but by first asking what God wants me to do. When we are willing to set apart time to seek God, the Holy Spirit guides us in the right direction and gives us strength to complete what he has entrusted to us.
a: Draw near to God each morning before you get busy
The fruitfulness of a day begins in the morning. Let God’s word and prayer be the first breath of your spirit.
Let God’s will, not people’s needs, guide you
Don’t be pulled along by applause, expectations, and pressure. Learn from Jesus to seek the Father’s sending first and then act.
Treat service as a mission, not a performance
Jesus preached and cast out demons to fulfill the purpose for which he was sent, not to please people, but to bring God’s Kingdom among them.
q: Am I willing to set apart time each day to draw near to God first? Is my service coming from God’s sending, or from people’s expectations?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving us an example, so that from Jesus I can learn what true priorities are. Help me to be willing every day to set apart time to seek You, and let Your will guide my every step. May I not be carried away by the voices of people, but follow Your sending alone. May everything I do be for the glory of Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Hear the Lord’s Call and Boldly Answer His Love
v: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall. He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.
My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”
My dove, in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.
b: This passage from the Song of Solomon is a picture full of love and invitation. The beloved comes across mountains and hills and stands outside the window, calling to his dear one: “Rise up… and come away” (2:10). This is God’s call to his people: come out of the spiritual winter and into the spring of walking with him; come out of hiding and into the embrace of his love.

The picture of “he stands behind our wall, glancing through the lattice” (2:9) shows us: **God longs to be near us, but he does not force us. He waits for our hearts to open so that he can meet us.** He not only calls, he paints a scene full of life and joy: flowers blooming and fruit ripening, a picture of the season of abundance he has prepared for us (2:11–13).

But this passage also warns us: “Catch for us the little foxes” (2:15). The little foxes stand for the small things in life that quietly spoil relationships, such as a cold heart, unresolved hurt, and neglecting the Lord in our busyness. If they are not dealt with in time, they will ruin the love and trust that are growing.

When we hear God’s gentle voice and feel his steadfast love, let us not hide any longer, but boldly answer his call. He wants us to come out and walk with him, leave behind the shadows of the past, and enter a renewed season of walking with him.
a: Open your heart and listen closely for the Lord’s call
He is calling from outside the window: “Rise up, and come away!” Are you willing to put down your hesitation and coldness and move toward him?
Take a bold step of faith into the new season God has prepared for you
Don’t stay trapped in “winter” any longer. Your spiritual life is blooming in spring, and walking with the Lord brings renewal and breakthrough.
Watch out for the “little foxes”
Guard your heart carefully, so that small compromises don’t damage the love and relationship that are bearing fruit between you and God.
q: Am I hiding? Am I willing to answer God’s invitation and rise up to walk with him? Are there little foxes hiding in my life that spoil spiritual fruit?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for crossing every barrier to come to me and softly call me to walk with You. Help me to open the door of my heart, no longer shrinking back or hiding, but boldly answering Your love. Shine Your light also on the little foxes in my life that harm my relationship with You, so that I may deal with them quickly and keep close to You. May my life be full of fruit in Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Hold to the Truth Without Backing Down, Even If It Costs You
v: It happened, as we were going to prayer, that a certain girl having a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by fortune telling.
Following Paul and us, she cried out, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to you the way of salvation!”
She did this for many days. But Paul, becoming greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!” It came out that very hour.
But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas, and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.
When they had brought them to the magistrates, they said, “These men, being Jews, are agitating our city,
and are teaching customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or to observe, being Romans.”
The multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates tore their clothes off of them, and commanded them to be beaten with rods.
When they had laid many stripes on them, they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely,
who, having received such a command, threw them into the inner prison, and secured their feet in the stocks.
b: When Paul and Silas were preaching in Philippi, they cast an evil spirit out of a slave girl, and her owners lost their income. They were accused and brought before the authorities. They were not suffering for any sin; they suffered because they had done what was right, yet they were falsely accused, beaten, and thrown into prison. This passage shows us that standing for the truth does not always bring immediate applause; sometimes it brings persecution and shame.

Truth and profit often cannot coexist. When the gospel interferes with people’s selfish plans, resistance appears. Paul did not compromise. By the wisdom and authority that came from God, he rebuked the powers of darkness and set a captive life free. What he relied on was not his own ability but the Lord who rules heaven and earth.

In this hardship, Paul and Silas chose to endure and hold on to the end, because they knew that God’s will is higher than human judgment, and that God’s presence is greater than the darkness of circumstances. Like those who feared God in ancient times and followed the guidance of the law and the prophets, they would rather suffer than turn away from the Most High God.
a: Discern spiritual things and don’t be taken in by words that sound devout
Even when words sound right, test the spirit behind them to see whether it is from God.
Hold on to your faith under persecution and don’t be shaken by fear
Our identity is that we are God’s servants. Facing the pressure of the world, stand firm in faith on the word of God.
Believe that God still reigns in the darkness
Even when you are in a tight spot, if you keep your eyes fixed on him, God will never leave or forsake you, and he will deliver you in his time.
q: When my faith is challenged, am I willing to stand on the side of truth? Am I willing to bear misunderstanding and rejection from people for God’s name?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for letting me see a faithful example in Paul and Silas. Even under persecution, they held to the mission You gave them. Give me also courage and a steady heart, not to compromise before the truth and to keep trusting in trouble. May my life bring You glory, in good times and hard, walking in the way that pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: A Woman Who Fears God Is a Blessing and Glory to Her Home
v: Who can find a worthy woman? For her price is far above rubies.
The heart of her husband trusts in her. He shall have no lack of gain.
She does him good, and not harm, all the days of her life.
She seeks wool and flax, and works eagerly with her hands.
She is like the merchant ships. She brings her food from afar.
She rises also while it is still night, and gives food to her household, and portions for her servant girls.
She considers a field, and buys it. With the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.
She girds her loins with strength, and strengthens her arms.
She perceives that her merchandise is profitable. Her lamp doesn’t go out by night.
b: In these words of wisdom we see a true picture of a woman of worth. She is not merely a symbol of beauty or gentleness, but a woman who fears God, who is wise and hardworking, and who gives her whole heart to building up her family and society. Her life is active, full of responsibility and perseverance. She does not simply care for her family; she brings them stability and hope.

Her worth does not lie in worldly labels but in putting God’s principles into practice in daily life. She respects her husband and lets him rely on her with peace of mind (31:11). She manages diligently and returns what she earns to the family (31:16). She does not save up for herself, but plans and gives for the good of the whole household. This is a selfless way of living: not for personal reputation, but to glorify God and bless her family.

This woman also knows how to seize the moment and work without letting up. She “rises while it is still night” and “her lamp doesn’t go out by night” (31:15, 18), showing that she invests herself in each day, making her life a source of strength and direction for her family. She is fear of God in action, and the foundation of a wise household.
a: Build a life of influence, whether you are a husband, a wife, or single
The woman of worth is a model not only for sisters but for all believers: fear God, and manage life with diligence and wisdom.
Put your faith into practice in daily life
Don’t wait for big events to depend on God. Let God’s principles guide you in every meal, every expense, and every decision.
Offer your abilities to God and be a blessing to your family and others
The woman of worth does not pile up gains for herself; her whole household benefits from her. This is exactly what selflessness looks like.
q: Like this woman of worth, do I let my faith enter my daily choices and actions? Am I willing to offer my abilities as a vessel God can use in my family and in society?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving us the example of the woman of worth, so that I can see how those who fear You shine in daily life. Help me, in whatever role I have, to live out my faith with diligence, wisdom, and love, and to bring an influence that glorifies You to my family, church, and society. May I spend my life doing what pleases You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Look to God in Trouble: He Is the Shield Around Me
v: (A Psalm by David, when he fled from Absalom his son.) Yahweh, how they are increased who distress me! Many are they who rise up against me.
Many there are who say of my soul, “There is no help for him in God.” (Selah.)
But you, Yahweh, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
I cry to Yahweh with my voice, and he answers me out of his holy hill. (Selah.)
I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for Yahweh sustains me.
I will not be afraid of tens of thousands of people who have set themselves against me on every side.
Arise, Yahweh! Save me, my God! For you have struck all my enemies on the cheek bone. You have broken the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to Yahweh. May your blessing be on your people. (Selah.)
b: David wrote this psalm in one of his darkest hours. He was facing the rebellion of his son Absalom, friends had abandoned him, enemies surrounded him, and many even concluded that “there is no help for him in God.” Yet at this low point in his life, David did not give up, and he did not strike back in his own way. He chose to turn his eyes to Yahweh and call on his name.

He said, “You, Yahweh, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head” (3:3). In human eyes he had lost power, lost hope, and even failed; but in God’s eyes he was still a servant God loved. Real security is not armies or power; it is God himself being the shield around you.

David could “lay down and sleep, and awaken” in the middle of a war, unafraid, because he knew God was watching over him (3:5–6). This is the peace and trust that grow in a heart that fears God in hard times. When we hand authority back to God and no longer rely on our own cleverness and temper, we can experience his saving work.
a: Under pressure and betrayal, choose to look to God instead of complaining about people
Like David, when people misunderstand and attack you, let your first response be to turn to God, not to fight back in your own way.
Believe that God is the shield around you
However many enemies there are and however dangerous the circumstances, if God is with you, nothing can overcome you.
Let God be the source of your glory
Not by your performance, and not by people’s praise, but by letting God’s presence, protection, and answers be your inner security.
q: Under pressure, am I quick to protect myself rather than turn to God? Do I believe that even when everything seems out of control, God is still my shield and my help?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not leaving me even when I am surrounded on every side. Though many misunderstand and persecute me, You are the shield around me and the glory in my heart. Teach me in hard times to lean on You, to lift up my head with courage, and to be sure that salvation belongs to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Failure Is Not the End; Turn Back and You Can Begin Again
v: All the people said to Samuel, “Pray for your servants to Yahweh your God, that we not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for ourselves a king.”
Samuel said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. You have indeed done all this evil; yet don’t turn away from following Yahweh, but serve Yahweh with all your heart.
Don’t turn away to go after vain things which can’t profit or deliver, for they are vain.
For Yahweh will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake, because it has pleased Yahweh to make you a people for himself.
Moreover as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against Yahweh in ceasing to pray for you; but I will instruct you in the good and the right way.
Only fear Yahweh, and serve him in truth with all your heart; for consider what great things he has done for you.
But if you still do wickedly, you will be consumed, both you and your king.”
b: When the people of Israel realized their mistake in asking for a king, they feared God’s judgment and asked Samuel to pray for them. This shows how our hearts so often drift from God, choosing to depend on visible power rather than on the unseen Lord who reigns. But through Samuel, God gave great comfort: “Don’t be afraid… serve Yahweh with all your heart.” In other words, if they are willing to turn back, God is still willing to receive them and lead them to begin again.

This passage reveals three foundational truths. God is faithful, and for his name’s sake he does not forsake us. God’s word and guidance are the standard for our lives, and only on his right path do we find peace. And fearing him and relying on him wholeheartedly is the road we are to walk every day. Even if we have drifted or been weak, what decides the future is not past mistakes but whether we now turn back to fear God and serve him truly.

Samuel was not only an intercessor but also a spiritual guide. By his actions he reminds us that those who fear God do not only hold on to their own faith; they are also willing to lead others back onto the right path and help them realign with God’s heart. This is the witness of a life that lets God be King and gives him the glory.
a: If you feel you have made a wrong decision, now is the time to turn back
God does not ask you to be perfect, only to be willing to come back sincerely; he is always waiting to receive the repentant.
Stop following false and powerless sources of security; fix your eyes on Yahweh
What the world offers to lean on is empty in the end. Only God’s word and his presence are real security.
Become an intercessor and an example in others’ lives
Like Samuel, don’t only keep to the right path yourself, but help those around you return to God’s way.
q: Am I willing to let go of past wrong choices and truly turn back? Am I willing to let God’s will rule my life again?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not treating me according to my past mistakes, but calling me back with Your loving kindness. Help me to fear You wholeheartedly and no longer depend on empty things. Let me walk every day in the path that pleases You, and let me be someone who leads others back to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Open Your Heart to See the Lord’s Glory, and Be Changed From Glory to Glory
v: But if the service of death, written engraved on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face, which was passing away,
won’t service of the Spirit be with much more glory?
For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.
For even that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.
For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.
Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,
and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face, that the children of Israel wouldn’t look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.
But their minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.
But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.
But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.
b: This passage sharply contrasts the glory of the old covenant law with the glory of the Spirit in the new covenant. When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, his face shone from having seen God’s glory, so much that people could not look at him directly. But that glory was fading. Now, in Christ, we no longer need a veil to cover it; we can open our hearts boldly and without fear to see the Lord’s glory directly and be changed by it.

What God gives is not rules that bring death, but the Spirit who gives life. When we let God be the example, standard, and guide of our lives, we are renewed daily in his light and continually shaped into his image. This is not done by our own effort at imitation, but by the Lord’s Spirit dwelling in us and transforming us, so that our life changes from the old self to the new self, and from a self-centered life into the glory of selflessness.

Paul reminds us that when our hearts turn to the Lord, the veil is taken away. The question is not whether God’s glory is shown, but whether we open ourselves to let him shine on us. Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom: freedom from condemnation and from self, and into truth and life.
a: Open your heart and draw near to God without hiding
God longs to let us see his glory, but he does not force it. We have to take the initiative to open the door of our hearts and let his true light in.
Let God’s word and the Holy Spirit shape our inner life every day
Not outward form, but inner renewal, so that we become more and more like the Lord.
Change your life not by your own effort but by the transforming work of the Lord’s Spirit
True freedom is release from the inside out, the result of the Lord’s Spirit working within us.
q: Is there still a veil over my heart, keeping me from facing God’s light? Am I willing to let the Holy Spirit work freely in my life, so that I am changed from glory to glory?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that through Jesus I can see Your glory with an unveiled face. Remove the veil from my heart, so that I no longer run away or cover myself, but open myself and let Your Spirit change me. May my life be renewed every day by You, becoming more and more like You, to the glory of Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Long for God’s Presence and Find True Satisfaction in Your Spirit
v: God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.
So I have seen you in the sanctuary, watching your power and your glory.
Because your loving kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise you.
So I will bless you while I live. I will lift up my hands in your name.
My soul shall be satisfied as with the richest food. My mouth shall praise you with joyful lips,
when I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches.
For you have been my help. I will rejoice in the shadow of your wings.
My soul stays close to you. Your right hand holds me up.
But those who seek my soul to destroy it shall go into the lower parts of the earth.
They shall be given over to the power of the sword. They shall be jackal food.
But the king shall rejoice in God. Everyone who swears by him will praise him, for the mouth of those who speak lies will be silenced.
b: This psalm is a prayer David wrote in the wilderness of Judah. He was in a place of thirst in body and soul, with no help on any side, yet he showed a deep longing for God. He did not ask that his circumstances be changed; he earnestly sought God himself. David understood that what truly satisfies the soul is not outward comfort but the sweetness of God’s presence. He said, “Your loving kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise you.” This is spiritual clarity and longing, so that even in the wilderness a person can be satisfied in God.

This passage expresses a God-centered attitude of life that wants God to be King. David was not merely trying to survive; in the night he thought about God and lifted his hands in worship, his soul satisfied as with the richest food. He did not fix his gaze on circumstances or enemies, but chose to cling to God, letting God’s right hand be his real security. This is a life that belongs to God, one that gives God the glory and lives under his guidance.

In the end, David placed both judgment and victory in God’s hands. He believed that God would vindicate him and bring justice. That is why he could shout for joy in hardship and praise in the wilderness: he knew that as long as God was with him, his spirit would never thirst again.
a: Keep a longing for God in your spirit, even in a dry place
When circumstances are hard, fix your eyes all the more on God and turn the desire of your heart toward him, not toward substitutes.
Let God’s loving kindness satisfy your soul
Don’t let the pursuits of life take the place of God. His presence is the only spring that can truly feed your soul.
Connect with God daily through prayer and praise
Morning and night, think of God, remember him, and bless him, and let him be your strength and direction every day.
q: When my soul feels weary, am I willing, like David, to earnestly seek God? Is God truly the One I long for most each day?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, my heart longs for You, as a dry and waterless land longs for a spring. Draw me to Yourself, so that I seek You every day and take Your loving kindness as the deepest satisfaction of my life. May I not be frightened by hard times or let circumstances steal my joy, but rejoice in the shadow of Your wings. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: To Believe in Jesus Is to Have Life, Moving From Doubt to Assurance
v: This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and with the blood. It is the Spirit who bears witness, because the Spirit is truth.
For there are three who bear witness:
the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and the three agree as one.
If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater; for this is the witness of God which he has testified concerning his Son.
He who believes in the Son of God has the witness in himself. He who doesn’t believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the witness that God has given concerning his Son.
The witness is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.
These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.
b: This passage brings us back to a fundamental question: how do I know I really have eternal life? The answer is not feelings and not performance, but whether you have Jesus. God testifies in agreement through the water (Jesus’ baptism), the blood (his cross), and the Holy Spirit, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and the source of life.

If we truly believe that Jesus is Lord and Savior, then this witness from God becomes assurance in our hearts. We do not prove we are saved by living a good life through our own effort; it is because the Son of God lives in us that we have the life that belongs to God. This life is no longer lived for ourselves, but lets Jesus live in us, following his will, submitting to the Holy Spirit’s leading, and glorifying God’s name.

A life that belongs to God is built on God’s promises, and it grows steadier as we walk with him. It does not rest on human enthusiasm or religious activity alone, but on depending on Jesus every day, doing what he says, and letting him reign. In this life, our identity is no longer unclear: we know that we are children of God, heirs of eternal life.
a: Put down doubt and believe that God’s witness is truer than human voices
Don’t let feelings sway your confidence in salvation. God has testified clearly: in Christ there is eternal life.
Stay connected to Jesus every day and live out the new life he gives
Read God’s word and listen to the Holy Spirit’s guidance, so that your life is no longer lived for yourself but for God.
Be sure in your heart that you are a child of God, and stop wavering
This assurance will become the strength to resist temptation and hold to the truth, and it will help you live a life that glorifies God.
q: Do I believe that Jesus has finished everything for me? Do I let this assurance of life become the foundation of my faith and actions every day?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for accomplishing salvation for me through Jesus, so that I can be sure I have eternal life. Help me to connect with Jesus every day, not relying on my own effort but living the life that belongs to You by Your Spirit. Let me live clearly, steadily, and in a way that glorifies Your name. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Be Ready to Meet the Lord; Don’t Wait for God Empty-Handed
v: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins, who took their lamps, and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
Those who were foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them,
but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
Now while the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.
But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Behold! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.
The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’
But the wise answered, saying, ‘What if there isn’t enough for us and you? You go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’
While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut.
Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’
But he answered, ‘Most certainly I tell you, I don’t know you.’
Watch therefore, for you don’t know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.”
b: This parable is Jesus’ teaching about the Kingdom of heaven, and an important call to all believers. All ten virgins took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom. They looked alike and had the same goal, but the difference was whether they had prepared oil. The wise ones had prepared in advance for the possible delay. The foolish had prepared only on the surface, and when the crucial moment came, it showed how little real life lay inside them.

This parable reveals a key to a life that belongs to God: whether we are truly preparing ourselves to meet the Lord. The lamp stands for witness, and the oil for the life of the Holy Spirit and a lasting practice of faith. Some people look devout and seem zealous outwardly, but if they lack inner reality and a long walk with God, then when the Lord comes, they will be found empty, with no time to make up for it.

A life that belongs to God is not on the surface, and it is not last-minute cramming. Each day, in faith, we store up oil, led by the Holy Spirit, living a life that lets Jesus be King and glorifies God. It is not about busily pleasing people, but about living alert, in step with the Lord. When the Lord comes and the door is shut, the opportunity is gone. The point is not whether you want to go in, but whether you are ready to sit at the feast with the Lord.
a: Store up spiritual oil every day and stay close to the Lord
Don’t just look like a Christian. Truly spend time with God and experience the renewing and guidance of the Holy Spirit.
Don’t depend on someone else’s faith; have your own preparation
Oil can’t be borrowed and faith can’t be copied. You must take responsibility for your own life and faith.
Let the Lord’s return be the motivation and focus of your life
Not waiting passively, but actively living in reverence for God, obeying him, and serving others until he comes.
q: Am I living today in preparation to meet the Lord? Is there enough oil in my lamp? If the Lord came right now, could I meet him with confidence?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give me a watchful heart. Let me be devout not only on the outside, but truly store up spiritual oil within, renewed day by day by Your Spirit. Help me to live the life that pleases You, so that at the moment of Your return I will not be caught in panic, but will joyfully enter Your feast. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Don’t Listen to the Voice of Temptation; Hold Tightly to God’s Word
v: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”
The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,
but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it, neither shall you touch it, lest you die.’”
The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,
for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate; and she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate.
b: This passage records the beginning of humanity’s fall, and reveals the nature of temptation and the fragility of the human heart. Satan, in the form of a serpent, did not use violence but a seemingly harmless question: “Has God really said…?” This one sentence began to shake people’s trust in God’s word, moving the focus from God’s goodness to our own desires.

Eve knew God’s command, but in the conversation she gradually lost focus and distorted it, changing “do not eat” into “do not eat, and do not touch.” This exposed her incomplete trust in God’s word and the uncertainty in her heart. Once the heart loosens, lies find their opening. The serpent went further: “You won’t really die,” and even tempted them to believe that God was “hiding good things.” So people began replacing God’s standard with their own, using “it looks good” to decide “whether it should be done.”

This is the very trap we often fall into today: we easily listen to the voice of the world and the voice of our feelings instead of obeying God’s voice alone. When we leave God-centered thinking, temptation takes control. A life that belongs to God does not do what looks pleasing in its own eyes; it takes God’s word as the standard, relies on the Holy Spirit’s guidance, and gives Satan’s lies no opening.
a: Build a right understanding of God’s word; truth is the shield against temptation
Read and meditate on Scripture daily, so that you know God’s word well and clearly and can stand firm when temptation comes.
When doubts arise, return to God’s heart rather than your own reasoning
Satan most often uses not obvious lies but half-truths and twisted logic. Begin from God’s word to discern.
In every choice, let God be King, not your feelings
Don’t ask whether it benefits you; ask whether it fits God’s heart.
q: Do I often let feelings and outward attractions influence my choices? When facing temptation, am I able to stand firm in the Lord?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, give me a clear understanding of Your word and a deep trust in it. Don’t let me be led astray by doubt and lies, but let me center every choice on You. Help me not to walk by sight or feelings, but to obey Your guidance in faith. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Hold to What Is Pure in the Midst of Chaos; Live Gently in the Midst of Argument
v: Remind them of these things, charging them in the sight of the Lord that they not argue about words to no profit, to the subverting of those who hear.
Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, a workman who doesn’t need to be ashamed, properly handling the word of truth.
But shun empty chatter, for it will proceed further in ungodliness,
Flee from youthful lusts, but follow after righteousness, faith, love, and peace, with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
But refuse foolish and ignorant questionings, knowing that they generate strife.
The Lord’s servant must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient,
in gentleness correcting those who oppose him: perhaps God may give them repentance leading to a full knowledge of the truth,
and they may recover themselves out of the devil’s snare, having been taken captive by him to his will.
b: Paul reminded the young Timothy that in pastoring and teaching the church, knowledge is not enough; one needs a life that belongs to God. Facing worldly talk and pointless debates, God’s servant does not argue to prove himself, but reveals the truth with a pure attitude and by rightly handling God’s word.

A life that lets God be King is willing to stay away from selfish desires, and with those who follow the Lord from a pure heart to pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, without falling into emotional and verbal confrontation. What truly transforms hearts is not our power to persuade, but the work of the Holy Spirit and the gift of repentance God gives.

A life that belongs to God shows itself in an attitude that does not quarrel, but responds to hostility and opposition with gentleness, patience, and reverence. Such a life lives by God’s standard, does not fall into human arguments or Satan’s snares, and instead becomes a vessel in the Lord’s hands with witness and influence.
a: In conflict, choose humility and yielding, not arguing and emotion
Not every topic deserves a reply. Knowing when to keep silent and keep away is a mark of wisdom.
Take root in the truth and be a worker with nothing to be ashamed of
Keep learning God’s word and rightly handle the word of truth, so that you are not misled by distorted teaching.
Use gentleness and patience to be a witness that transforms others’ lives
Attitude speaks louder than words. If your life reflects God’s character, people will be willing to listen about the God you believe in.
q: Have I ever argued with someone just to prove I was right? When facing mistakes and opposition, do I respond with gentleness and patience?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, help me to be a worker after Your own heart, who speaks not to argue but lives for the truth. Teach me to be careful in my words and gentle in my attitude, relying not on myself but on the life and wisdom You give, to influence and transform hearts. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Trust Jesus in the Waiting, and Believe He Is Life Even in Disappointment
v: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister, Martha.
It was that Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother, Lazarus, was sick.
The sisters therefore sent to him, saying, “Lord, behold, he for whom you have great affection is sick.”
But when Jesus heard it, he said, “This sickness is not to death, but for the glory of God, that God’s Son may be glorified by it.”
Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
When therefore he heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was.
Then after this he said to the disciples, “Let’s go into Judea again.”
So when Jesus came, he found that he had already been in the tomb four days.
Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
Many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.
Then when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house.
Therefore Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.
Even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”
Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”
Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me, though he dies, yet will he live.”
b: Lazarus’s grave illness, his death, and Jesus’ “delay” became a source of great confusion and struggle. Martha and Mary both knew Jesus and believed in his power, but in their pain and waiting their faith was tested. Yet Jesus said, “This sickness is not to death, but for the glory of God.” His vision goes beyond what people see in reality, and his works always follow his own timetable.

Jesus’ delay was not coldness; it came out of his deep love, in order to bring about greater grace and revelation. He wanted to lead Martha into a new knowledge: not only to believe that God can change circumstances, but to believe that Jesus himself is the resurrection and the life. This is a God-centered view of life: no longer judging God’s love by results, but choosing to trust him even in waiting and disappointment.

We are often like Martha: we believe God “can,” but we doubt why he doesn’t start working right away. True faith is believing, before he acts, that his work will bring glory and life. This kind of life is centered on Jesus, takes his timing and his ways as the standard, and, led by the Holy Spirit, learns to say without wavering in hard times, “Lord, you are still the one I trust.”
a: When God seems “late,” don’t rush to disappointment; wait for his timing and arrangement
God’s delay is never forgetfulness. It is for greater glory and deeper training in faith.
Believe that Jesus is not only able to do miracles; he himself is life
He is not bringing news of resurrection; he is the resurrection, the source of hope you can live out every day.
Learn to respond to reality with faith, not walking by sight but living by trust in God. Is your faith still firm even when you have not yet seen the answer to your prayer?
q: When I face waiting and disappointment, do I still believe in Jesus’ presence and faithfulness? Am I willing to trust his timing, his ways, and his heart?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I feel confused and disappointed in waiting, help me, like Martha, to say, “Lord, I know that whatever You ask, God will do.” Let me walk not by sight but by faith, holding tightly to Jesus, for he is my resurrection and my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.

t: Live Each Day in God’s Will and Let Your Life Be a Vessel That Pleases Him
v: Always rejoice.
Pray without ceasing.
In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus toward you.
Don’t quench the Spirit.
Don’t despise prophesies.
Test all things, and hold firmly that which is good.
Abstain from every form of evil.
May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely. May your whole spirit, soul, and body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Faithful is he who calls you, who will also do it.
b: This passage is Paul’s very practical spiritual guidance for believers’ daily lives. It is not about accomplishing a grand ministry, but about living a life that walks with God every day. God’s will is not a hidden mystery; it is shown concretely in our daily choices: always rejoice, pray without ceasing, give thanks in everything.

These three are not moods but a way of life connected to Jesus. Joy is not because things go smoothly, but because our Lord still reigns. Prayer is not a formality but an ongoing, intimate conversation with God. Thanksgiving is not only for when good things happen; it is trusting that God’s hand is still leading even when circumstances have not changed.

When we live this way, we will not quench the Spirit, and we will not grow cold toward God’s word. We will learn to test everything, neither drifting by our feelings nor blindly following what others say, but holding firmly to all that is good and staying away from all that is evil. This is exactly what it looks like to let Jesus be King and let him be glorified.

Paul’s closing prayer is “May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely.” This reminds us that sanctification does not come from our own discipline or effort; God himself does the work. Since he has called us, he will also fulfill his purpose. As long as we are willing to cooperate with his leading, he will keep our spirit, soul, and body whole and blameless until the Lord returns.
a: Practice joy, prayer, and thanksgiving in daily life
This is not just a Sunday exercise; it is a habit that can be lived out every day at home, at work, and in relationships.
Be sensitive to the Holy Spirit’s promptings and love God’s word
Don’t let busyness, indifference, or criticism and judgment drown out what God wants to say to you. Keep a soft heart.
Let God govern your whole person and whole heart, so that you are blameless before the Lord
God’s goal is not to make you look good, but to make you like Jesus. Be willing to let him shape every part of you.
q: Am I living out God’s will in my daily life? Am I willing to let God change me himself, so that I become a vessel for his glory?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for not only giving me commands but for helping me live out Your will Yourself. Remind me every day to rejoice, pray, and give thanks; and sanctify me Yourself, so that my spirit, soul, and body may all please You. May my whole life be a witness to Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
